Ἶρις, ιδος, ἡ, acc. Ἶριν, voc. Ἶρι:—Iris, the messenger of the gods among themselves, Il. 8.398 (never in Od. ), Hes. Th. 780 , etc. (Perh. fr. Ϝῖρις, cf. ὠκέα Ἶρις Il. 2.786 , al., Hes. l.c.; ὦκα δὲ Ἶρις Il. 23.198 (Pap.); possibly also fr. Ἐϝῖρις: Εἶρις is…
the same number of times, as many times

ἴσᾱμι, v. Εἴδω (B), and add: ἴσᾱμι Theoc. 5.119 ; ἴσαις (2 sg.) Id. 14.34 ; ἴσᾱτι Id. 15.146 ; ἴσᾰτε Periand. ap. D.L. 1.99 ; ἴσαντι Theoc. 15.64 ; inf. γισάμεναι (i.e. ϝις-): εἰδέναι, Hsch. ; Arc. ἰσάμεν (ισμεν lapis), IG 5(2).357.12 ; 3 pl. subj. ἴσαντι…
change one with another, do in turn
Σπανίαν ( v.l. Ἱσπανίαν ) ὀνομαζομένην Id. 6.613 , cf. 12.428 , D.S. 5.37 .
bring to a standstill, stay, check
give an account of what one has learnt, record
written account of one's inquiries, narrative, history
doubtless, by all means, of course
—have no care for, be neglectful of
Ἴτυς, υος, ὁ, Itys, son of Tereus and Procne, A. Ag. 1144 (lyr.), Ar. Av. 212 , etc. [ῐτῠ-, but ἃ Ἴτῠν αἰὲν Ἴτῡν ὀλοφύρεται S. El. 148 (lyr.), cf. Ar. l.c.]

ἀμεμφ-ής, ές, mostly in pass. sense, = ἄμεμπτος 1 , IG 12(3).1075 (Melos), Pi. O. 6.46 , A. Pers. 168 , Supp. 581 ; in epitaph, Εὔκλειαν ἀ. Ἀρχ. Ἐφ. 1910.66 (Piraeus):—poet. and late Prose, Plu. Cim. 2 , Jul. Or. 2.99a . Act. , = ἄμεμπτος 11 , Plu. 2.610e ;…

ἰχθῦς (so Hdn.Gr. 2.936 , -ῦς and -ύς freq. in codd.), ύος, ὁ, acc. ἰχθύν Pi. Fr. 306 , cf. Hdn.Gr. 1.416 , Choerob. in Theod. 1.383 , in late Poets also ἰχθύα AP 9.227 (Bianor), Theoc. 21.45 : voc. ἰχθύ Erinn. 1 , Crates Com. 14 : pl. ἰχθύες Pl. Phd. 109e ,…

κᾱ, Dor. for Ep. , Aeol. κε(ν),= Att. , Arc. ἄν, SIG 9 (Olympia, vi B.C.), Epich. 35 ,al., Leg.Gort. 1.9 , Foed.Delph.Pell. 2 A 9 , Ar. Ach. 737 , 799 , Lys. 117 , Th. 5.77 , Theoc. 1.4 . [Although long, the α is elided in Epich. 170.12 ,al., SIG 56.8 (Argos,…

κᾰ, shortd. form of κατά used before the article, κα τὸν νόμον IG 5 ( 2 ). 16 (Arcadia); κα τῶννυ ib. 262 ; κα τοὺς νόμους SIG 2860.9 (Delph., ii B.C.), etc.; κα τὰ τῆς συγκλήτου δόγματα SIG 705.12 (ibid.) κα τὰ δόξαντα . . τῇ βουλῇ Inscr.Magn. 179.33 (ii…
κἀγώ [ᾱ], Att. crasis for καὶ ἐγώ.
καθεστῶτα, ων, τά, neut. pl. pf. part. of καθίστημι.
act as guide, lead the way

ἀμετά-βλητος, ον, hyperdor. -ατος Philol. 21 , unchangeable, κόσμος l.c., cf. Arist. Metaph. 1019a27 ; ἄτομα καὶ ἀ. Epicur. Ep. 1p.7U. ; ἀ. εἰς ἄλλα Ti.Locr. 98c . unchanged, J. AJ 15.7.5 ; τὸ ἀμετάβλητον Plu. 2.1011a : Gramm., not inflected, A.D. Synt.…

ἀμετά-βολος, ον, = foreg., Plu. Mar. 42 . Music, without modulation, σύστημα Aristid.Quint. 1.8 , Bacch. Harm. 74 ; ἁρμονία Plu. 2.437d ἀμετά-γνωστος, ον, unalterable, implacable, μῖσος J. AJ 16.10.1 . not to be repented of, ἡδονή Max.Tyr. 1.4 .
to be set, set oneself down, settle
in so far as, according as
Conj., copulative, joining words and sentences, and; also Adv., even, also, just
καινέω, prob. misspelling for καινίζω in aor. 1 part. καινήσασα, PThead. 19.11 (iv A. D.).
use for the first time, handsel
καιρόω, καίρωμα, καίρωσις, καιρωστίς or καιρο-τρίς, v. καῖρος .
κἀκ, crasis for καὶ ἐκ. κάκα: κακία ἢ ὄρνεον, Hsch. κακάβη, ἡ, κάκαβος, ἡ, κακάβιον, τό, v. κακκ- .

κᾰκοπαθ-έω, fut. -παθήσομαι PLond. 1.98r73 (i/ii A.D.): pf. κεκακοπάθηκα Aen.Tact. 26.7 :—to be in ill plight, be in distress, Th. 1.78 , X. Mem. 2.1.17 , And. 2.26 , Lys. 6.28 , D. 18.146 ; πολλὰ κ. PCair.Zen. 93.17 (iii B.C.); τινι by or from a thing, τοῦ…
κᾰκοφρᾰδ-μοσύνη, ἡ, = foreg., Democr. 273 , Orph. Fr. 285.41 (pl.).
precious stone of a greenish blue, turquoise
κάλλιστος, η, ον, Sup. of καλός; v. καλός B.
καλλοσύνη, Dor. καλλι-σύνα, ἡ, poet. for κάλλος, in lyr., E. Or. 1386 , Hel. 383 ; also eleg., Supp.Epigr. 1.570 ; κ. ἐπέων, title of work by Democr.
ἄμμες, Aeol. and Ep. for ἡμεῖς: acc. ἄμμε: gen. ἀμμέων: dat. ἄμμι( νρπαρ; Hom. , etc.; ἄμμεσιν, Alc. 100 . ἀμμέσον, poet. for ἀνὰ μέσον, Hes. ἀμμέτερος and ἄμμος, = ἡμέτερος , Alc. 105 A, B.
to be turned into smoke, burnt to ashes
κάρ, for κατά before ῥ, κὰρ ῥόον Il. 12.33 ; κάρ ῥα 20.421 .

Κάρ, ο, gen. Κᾱρός, pl. Κᾶρες ( contr. fr. Κᾰερ-), Carian, Il. 2.867 , etc.:—fem. Κάειρα [ᾰ] (q.v.): employed as mercenaries, καὶ δὴ 'πίκουρος ὥστε Κὰρ κεκλήσομαι Archil. 24 , cf. Ephor. 12 J. : hence prov., ἐν τῷ Καρὶ κινδυνεύειν (cf. experimentum facere in…
καρδιάω, = καρδιαλγέω , in Ep. part. καρδιόωντα, Nic. Al. 581 .
καρπέω, inf. καρπεῖν: πληώττειν, Hsch. κάρπη: τὰ σπέρματα: καὶ τήγανα ὀβελίσκους ἔχοντα, Id. κάρπημα, ατος, τό, gloss on καρπαλίον , Id.
in answer to, in accordance with
κατά, = κατὰ τά , IG 22.334.15 ; cf. κά. κᾆτα, Att. crasis for καὶ εἶτα, v. εἶτα sub fin. κατάβα, for κατάβηθι, aor. 2 imper. of καταβαίνω.

καταβιβρώσκω (pres. not found, v. ἐσθίω ), aor. κατέβρων h.Ap. 127 : pf. Pass. καταβέβρωμαι: aor. κατεβρώθην (v. infr.):—eat up, devour, h.Ap. l.c.; καταβεβρωκὼς σιτία ἴσως ἐλεφάντων τεττάρων Antiph. 82 : metaph., καταβεβρώκασι . . τὰς οὐσίας Hegesipp.Com.…
bowl in which the blood of victims was caught
have judgement given in one's favour
to be cast down, lose heart

καταιγ-ίς, ίδος, ἡ, ( αἰγίς 11 ) squall descending from above, hurricane, Democr. 14 , Arist. Mu. 395a5 , AP 7.273 ( Leon. ), Corn. ND 9 , Erot. s.v. πόνος , Gal. 18(2).178 , D.C. 74.12 , Lib. Or. 59.138 : metaph., of gusts of passion (cf. sq.), Phld. Herc.…

κατακαίω, Att. καταιτι-κάω [ᾱ], Ep. inf. κατακαιέμεν Il. 7.408 : fut. -καύσω Ar. Lys. 1218 : aor. κατέκαυσα Th. 7.25 ; Ep. 3 sg. κατέκηε Il. 6.418 ; 1 pl. subj. κατακήομεν ( v.l. -κείομεν ) Il. 7.333 ; inf. κατακῆαι Od. 11.46 , κακκῆαι ib. 74 ( v.l. -κεῖαι ):…

κατάκειμαι, Ep. 3 pl. κατακείαται Il. 24.527 : Ion. plpf. κατεκέατο Hdt. 7.229 ; subj. -κέωμαι Pl. Smp. 213b :— Pass. , only in pres. and impf. with fut. Med. -κείσομαι:—lie down, μῆλα τὰ δὴ κατάκειτ' ἐσφαγμένα Od. 10.532 ; ἐπὶ πλευρὰς κ. Il. 24.10 ; νέκυς κ.…

κατακτάομαι, fut. -κτήσομαι LXX 2 Ch. 28.10 :—get for oneself, win, κράτος, νοῦν, S. Aj. 768 , 1256 ; ἐγκλήματα, πλούτους, Th. 4.86 , Isoc. 4.182 : metaph., win over, gain completely, τὸ θέατρον Ael. VH 3.8 : aor. 2 Act. κατέκτην (as if from κατάκτημι) dub.…
ἀμοργός (B), ὁ, = ἀμοργίς , Cratin. 96 , cf. Paus.Gr. Fr. 47 , Harp.
recount, tell at length and in order
καταλιμπάνω, = καταλείπω , Hp. Mul. 1.78 , Th. 8.17 , Antiph. 35 , PPetr. 3pp.4,12 (iii B.C.), LXX Ge. 39.16 , Ocell. 4.13 , etc.
by way of conversation, in prose

ἁμός (A) or ἀμός [ᾱ], ή, όν, Aeol. ἄμμος Alc. 105 A, Milet. 3 No. 152.35 , = ἡμέτερος (cf. ὑμός for ὑμέτερος, σφός for σφέτερος, A.D. Pron. 111.18 ), freq. used for ἐμός, Il. 8.178 , Od. 11.166 , etc.; esp. in Dor. , Pi. P. 3.41 , 4.27 , Theoc. 5.108 ; Lacon.…

κατανᾱλ-ίσκω, impf. -ανάλισκον Isoc. 1.18 : plpf. -ανηλώκει (intr.) Pl. Ti. 36b : but aor. -ηνάλωσα Isoc. 9.60 :— Pass. , aor. -αναλωθῆναι Pl. Phd. 72d ; subj. -αναλωθῇ Hp. Epid. 2.4.1 ; indic. -ηναλώθησαν ib. 2 : pf. -ανήλωμαι Isoc. 3.31 codd.; inf.…
to be in one's right mind, in one's senses
make to come back, bring back

κατα-πλήσσω, Att. κατά-ττω, fut. -ξω D. 21.194 :—strike down, τινὸς εἰς τὴν κατακλεῖδα [ξίφος] PMag.Par. 1.300 : usu. metaph., strike with amazement, astound, terrify, κατέπλησσεν ἐπὶ τὸ φοβεῖσθαι Th. 2.65 ; ὁ φόβος κ. τὰς ψυχάς X. Cyr. 3.1.25 ; καταπλήξειν…

κατασκευ-άζω, fut. -σκευάσω, Att. -σκευῶ SIG 1097.9 (Athens, iv B.C.), IPE 12.32B53 (Olbia, iii B.C.): Dor. aor. -εσκεύαξα Ti. Locr. 94d , Test.Epict. 1.14 , also κατεσκέαξα Africa Italiana 1.330 (Cyrene): Boeot. aor. inf. -σκευάττη SIG 1185.13 (Tanagra, iii…

ἀμπλᾰκ-ία, and ἀμβλ- (v. infr.), ἡ, = ἀμπλάκημα , Thgn. 204 , Emp. 115 , Hp. Ep. 22 ; ἀμπλακίαισι φρενῶν Pi. P. 3.13 ; τίνος ἀμπλακίας ποινὰς ὀλέκει; A. Pr. 564 ; ἀμπλακίαισι τῶν πάροιθεν E. Hipp. 835 , cf. A.R. 4.1082 , Rhian. 1.20 .
lay down from oneself, put off, lay aside

κατα-τρίβω [ῑ], fut. -ψω X. Cyr. 8.4.36 : pf. - τέτρῐφα Isoc. (v. infr.):— Pass. , fut. - τρῐβήσομαι X. HG 5.4.60 :— rub down or away: hence, of clothes, wear out, ἀμφὶ πλευρῇσι δοράς Thgn. 55 , cf. Ar. Fr. 345 , Pl. Phd. 87c , Metrod. Fr. 55 : hence metaph.,…

καταφθείρω, fut. - φθερῶ Plu. 2.24o d:—destroy, bring to naught, στρατόν, πόλιν, ἔθνη, A. Pers. 345 , S. OT 331 , Pl. Lg. 697d , cf. Democr. 159 ; ἔργα νομήων Theoc. 25.122 ; κατέφθαρται ὄλβος A. Pers. 251 ; ἐπεὶ δέ χ' εἵκω οἴκαδις καταφθερείς in sorry…
καταφθῐνύθω [ῠ], = καταφθίω , h.Cer. 353 , Emp. 111.4 ; cf. sq.
κατα-φύγιον [ῠ], τό , Dim. of foreg., Democr. 180 , Sch. Hermog.in Rh. 4.172 W.
tell lies against, speak falsely of

κατ-ῑθύνω, Ion. and Ep. for κατευθύνω, κ. τὸν πλόον Hdt. 2.96 , cf. Hp. Art. 71 , Luc. Trag. 56 , Aristaenet. 1.15 ; κῦμα Mosch. 2.121 ; χεῖρα τοξότιν AP 6.188 ( Leon. ); ῥήματος ἁρμονίην APl. 4.226 ( Alc. ).
bring home and re-establish there, restore to one's country
initiate in orgies, prepare for them

κατ-ορύσσω, Att. κάτ-ττω, fut. Pass. -ορυχθήσομαι cj. in Antipho 3.2.10 , -ορῠχήσομαι cj. in Ar. Av. 394 (lyr.): pf. Pass. -ορώρυγμαι Antipho 3.3.12 , etc., later κατώρυγμαι LW 1075 (Apollonia ad Rhyndacum), Str. 9.3.8 , cf. Moer. p.240 P.: aor. 2 inf. Pass.…

κε, also κεν, Ep. , Lesb., Cypr. ( Inscr.Cypr. 135.10 H., al.), Thess. ( IG 9(2).517.13 , al. (Larissa)); always enclitic, = ἄν and κᾱ (qq.v.); οὐκ ἄν . . ἀλλά κεν Il. 13.290 ; οὐκ ἄν . . οὐδέ κε 19.272 , al.; both coupled, ἄν κεν 11.187 , Od. 5.361 , Parm.…
κεῖ, Adv., = κεῖθι, ἐκεῖθι , Archil. 170 , Herod. 1.26 .
to be laid up, in store
anything stored up as valuable, treasure, heirloom
κεῖνος, η , ο, Ion. and poet. for ἐκεῖνος. Adv. κείνως. κεινός, ή, όν, Ion. and poet. for κενός. κεινόω, v. κενόω . Κεῖος, v. Κέως . κεῖρα: γενεά, ἢ ἡλικία, Hsch.
κεντάω, late form of sq., Pass. inf. -ᾶσθαι (v.l. -εῖσθαι) Gal. 6.192 .

κεντ-έω, Pi. P. 1.28 , etc.: fut. -ήσω S. Aj. 1245 : aor. ἐκέντησα Hp. Epid. 5.45 , Dor. κέντᾱσα Theoc. 19.1 ; Ep. inf. κένσαι (as if from Κέντω) Il. 23.337 :— Pass. , fut. -ηθήσομαι (συγ-) Hdt. 6.29 : aor. ἐκεντήθην Arist. Spir. 483b16 , Thphr. HP 9.15.3 :…
κεντόω, v.l. for κεντρόω 1 in Hdt. 3.16 .
κεράς (A), άδος, ἡ, poet. fem. of κεραός, Eust. 1625.45 ; but in Hsch. , κεραΐδες: τῶν προβάτων τὰ θήλεα, τὰ ἔνδον ὀδόντας ἔχοντα.
κερατέα, ἡ, = κερατωνία , Gp. 11.1 ; dub. sens. in POxy. 2146.9 (iii A.D.), PGen. 75.8 (iii/iv A.D.).
critical mark to indicate corrupt passages
any taper rod, of wood, ivory
wedge-shaped division of the seats in the theatre
κέω, v. κείω . κεώδης: καθαρός, and κεώσατο: καθήρατο, Hsch. ; cf. κηώδης, κήϊα. κεῶεν ὄζει: εὐωδεῖ, Id. (Neut. of Κεώεις = κηώεις. )

Κέως, ἡ, Ceos, one of the Cyclades, IG 12(5).532.7 , Str. 10.5.6 , etc.:—hence Κεῖος, Ion. Κήϊος, ὁ, a Ceian, Hdt. 5.102 , etc.; οὐ Χῖος, ἀλλὰ Κεῖος not a (roguish) Chian, but an (honest) Ceian, proverb in Ar. Ra. 970 ; ἀκόλαστόν τινα . . , καὶ οὐδαμῶς Κεῖον…
that which is cried by a herald, proclamation
to be a herald, officiate as herald
κῐθᾰρῳδ-ία, ἡ, = foreg., Pl. Lg. 700d (pl.), Ion 533b .
one who plays and sings to the cithara
to be put in motion, go
Κίρκη, ἡ, Circe, Od. 10.136 , Hes. Th. 957 , etc.
division of the nostrils, cartilage of the nose
omen, presage contained in a chance utterance
that which is assigned by lot, allotment
a beetle destructive in bee-hives, Clerus apiarius
that on which one lies, couch
κλίτα: στοαί, ἢ σέλλας (ἐλαίας cod.) εἰς τὸ κατακλίνεσθαι, Hsch.
κλίτος [ῐ], εος, τό, = κλειτύς , Lyc. 600 ; cliff, Id. 737 (pl.). = κλίμα 11 , clime, κ. βόρειον AP 7.699 . side, LXX Ex. 26.18 , al.; τὸ κ. τὸ δεξιόν ib. Ez. 47.1 ; τὸ κ. τοῦ νότου ib. 3 Ki. 7.39 .
Κλωθώ, οῦς, ἡ, Spinster, one of the three Μοῖραι, who spins the thread of life (cf. Κλῶθες), Hes. Th. 218 , Sc. 258 , Pl. R. 617c , Luc. Hist. Conscr. 38 : late nom. pl. Κλωθῶες IG 14.1389i14 .
part between knee and ankle, leg, shank
use the language of common life
undertake together, make common cause in

κοινων-έω, fut. -ήσω Pl. R. 54o c: pf. κεκοινώνηκα Id. Phdr. 246d , etc.:— Pass. , fut. κοινωνήσομαι (v. infr.): pf. κεκοινώνημαι Id. Lg. 801e :—have or do in common with, share, take part in a thing with another, c. gen. rei et dat. pers., τῆς πολιτείας κ.…
κόλχος, ὁ, f.l. for κόχλος , AP 9.551 (pl., Antiphil. ), APl. 4.37 ( Leont. ).

Κόλχος, ὁ, Colchian, Hdt. 1.2 , etc.:—Adj. Κολχικός, ή, όν, Colchian, Id. 2.105 :—poet. also Κόλχος στόλος A.R. 4.485 :—fem. Κολχίς, ίδος, Hdt. 1.2 (but also Μηδείᾳ τῇ Κόλχῳ Pl. Euthd. 285c ): as Subst. Κολχίς (sc. γῆ), Colchis, Hdt. 1.104 , etc.; (sc. γυνή)…
carry away so as to preserve
κόμιον, τό, Dim. of κόμη, Arr. Epict. 2.24.24 , 3.22.10 . = προκόμιον , Dialex. 2.13 .
feast given on certain festivals to strangers

κόπρ-ιον, τό, = κόπρος , Id. Acut. 56 , Ruf. ap. Orib. 8.24.8 , PFay. 110.5 (i A. D.), etc.: pl., Heraclit. 96 , OGI 483.81 (Pergam.), Sor. 2.56 , Plu. Pomp. 48 . generally, dirt, filth, BGU 1115.50 (i B. C.); esp. in Magic, dirt taken from spot where a…

κόπτω, Od. 18.28 , etc.: fut. κόψω Hippon. 83 , Men. Pk. 64 , etc.: aor. ἔκοψα, Ep. κόψα Il. 13.203 : pf. κέκοφα (ἐκ-) X. HG 6.5.37 , (περι-) Lys. 14.42 , (συγ-) Pl. Tht. 169b ; Ep. part. κεκοπώς Il. 13.60 (v.l. -φώς, -πών), Od. 18.335 :— Med. , fut. κόψομαι…
κόρᾰκος, ὁ, a plaster, Paul.Aeg. 7.17 . pl., Scythian for φίλιοι δαίμονες, Luc. Tox. 7 .

κορέννῡμι, Them. Or. 16.213a ; κορεννύω, Gloss.; κορέω, Nic. Al. 195 ; κορέσκω, ib. 225 , 360 , 415 : fut. κορέσω Hdt. 1.212 ; Ep. κορέεις Il. 13.831 , κορέει 8.379 , 17.241 : aor. ἐκόρεσα 16.747 , A. Pr. 166 (lyr.); poet. ἐκόρεσσα Theoc. 24.138 , AP 7.204 (…
κορέω (B), v. κορέννυμι . κορζία, v. καρδία .

κόσμ-ιον, τό, Dim. (in form) of κόσμος, D.S. 25.15 , Plu. 2.141 d, BGU 1024 v 27 (iv A. D.); κ. ἡμέρας Secund. Sent. 5 ; τὰ τῆς ἀρχῆς κ. the insignia of office, D.S. 38 / 9.16 ; τὰ βασιλικὰ κ. Plu. Demetr. 45 ; στρατηγικά Id. Ant. 17 .
κόττος, ὁ, = ἀλεκτρυών , prob. in Ezek. Exag. 261 , cf. Hsch. ; also, horse, Id. a river-fish, Arist. HA 534a1 . = κύβος , Cod.Just. 1.4.25 ( 529 A. D. ).
κοῦρος (A), ὁ, Ep. and Ion. for κόρος (B) (q.v.).
loppings, twigs stripped from a tree

κράς, poet. form of κάρα, nom. only Simm. 4 ; gen. κρᾱτός Il. 5.7 , al., Trag. (v. infr.); dat. κρᾱτί Od. 9.490 , S. OC 313 , Ar. Ra. 329 , κράτεσφι Il. 10.156 ; acc. κρᾶτα Od. 8.92 , Trag. (v. infr.): pl., gen. κράτων Od. 22.309 ; dat. κρᾱσίν Il. 10.152 ;…
conquer, prevail, get the upper hand
become master of, get possession of
to be mightiest, best, most excellent

κρέας, τό, Dor. κρῆς (q.v.), Ep. κρεῖας dub. cj. in Anan. 5.3 ; Att. gen. κρέως S. Fr. 728 ; Cret. κρίως GDI 5128 (Vaxos): pl. κρέα IG 12.84.26 , etc.; gen. κρεῶν Od. 15.98 , Hdt. 1.73 , IG 12.10.7 , Ar. Ra. 191 , etc.; Ep. κρειῶν Il. 11.551 , al., κρεάων [ᾰ]…

Κρής, ὁ, gen. Κρητός, mostly in pl. Κρῆτες, ῶν , Cretan, Il. 2.645 , etc.: prov., ὁ Κρὴς τὸν πόντον (sc. ἀγνοεῖ), of those who feign ignorance, Alcm. 115 , cf. Str. 10.4.17 :—fem. Κρῆσσα, ης, Sapph. 54 : in pl., title of play by Aeschylus: as Adj., Cretan,…
κρούνωμα, ατος, τό, = κρουνός 2 , κ. βρότειον Emp. 6.3 .
serve as an attendant, tend, care for

κτάομαι, Ion. κτέομαι, only as v.l. in Hdt. 8.112 : fut. κτήσομαι Archil. 6.4 , Thgn. 200 , A. Eu. 289 , Th. 6.30 , Pl. R. 417a , etc. (in pass. sense, Plot. 2.9.15 , s.v.l.); κεκτήσομαι A. Th. 1022 , E. Ba. 514 , Pl. Grg. 467a (ἐκτήσομαι in La. 192e , and…

κτέᾰν-ον, τό , ̔κτάομαἰ = κτῆμα , Pi. P. 1.2 , Epic. ap. Sch. S. OC 378 ( Antim. (?)); κ. φιλίης, of a child, Epigr.Gr. 388 (Apamea). usu. in pl. κτέανα, possessions, property, Hes. Op. 315 , Sol. 4.12 , Pi. O. 3.42 , N. 9.32 ; δημοσίων κ. Xenoph. 2.8 ; used…
anything gotten, piece of property, possession
κτῠ́π-ημα, ατος, τό, = κτύπος, βροντῆς Critias 25.32 D. ; κ. τυμπάνων D.C. 51.17 , cf. Jul. Or. 7.220b ; κ. χειρός E. Andr. 1211 (lyr.).

κῡδρός, ά, όν , ̔κῦδος̓ = κυδάλιμος , in Hom. always in fem., as epith. of Hera and Leto, Διὸς κυδρὴ παράκοιτις Il. 18.184 , Od. 11.580 ; of Pallas, h.Hom. 28.1 ; Δίκη Hes. Op. 257 ( v.l. κυδνή ); θεαί, of the Nymphs, A. Fr. 168 (hex.); rarely of a mortal…

κῠέω, older and more Att. form of κύω, Il. 23.266 , etc. ( Aeol. (?) part. fem. κύεσσα Hsch. ; Arc. κύενσα IG 5(2).514.12 (Lycosura); Coan κυεῦσα Schwyzer 251 B 3 , written κυεοσα ib. A 61 (iv/iii B.C.)): impf. 3 sg. ἐκύει Il. 19.117 : fut. κυήσω Hp. Mul.…

Κύζῐκος, ἡ, Cyzicus, Hdt. 4.14 , etc., cf. Str. 12.8.11 :—Adj. Κυζικηνικός, ή, όν , βάμμα Ar. Pax 1176 :—more freq. Κυζικηνός, ή, όν, K. στατήρ a gold coin, Lys. 32.6 , D. 34.23 , etc.; without στ., Lys. 12.11 , X. An. 6.2.4 , D. 21.173 ; K. ἔμπλαστρος, name…
form a circle round, encompass, encircle
move in a circle, whirl round
place where the waves break, beach
hollow of a vessel: drinking-cup, bowl

ἀμφιτίθημι [τῐ], 3 sg. ἀμφιτιθεῖ Xenoph. 1.2 , imper. ἀμφιτίθει Thgn. 847 : aor. ind. ἀμφέθηκα, other moods supplied by aor. 2: (v. τίθημι):—put round, Hom. mostly in tmesi, ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ κυνέην κεφαλῆφιν ἔθηκεν Il. 10.261 , cf. Od. 13.431 ; τοῖς ἀδίκοις…
Κυρήνη, ἡ, Cyrene, Hdt. 4.162 , etc.:—Adj. Κυρηναῖος, α, ον, ib. 199 , etc. [ῠ in Hes. Fr. 128.2 , Pi. P. 4.2 , al., Call. Ap. 73 , 94 ; ῡ Ar. Th. 98 , A.R. 2.500 .]
κῡρι-όω, = κυρόω , dub. in Phld. Piet. 107 ( Pass. ).
Κῦρος, ὁ, Cyrus: ὁ πρότερος, the elder Cyrus, Hdt. 1.46 , etc. ὁ νεώτερος, the brother of Artaxerxes, X. An. 1.1.1 , etc.
κῶθος, ὁ, Sicel name for κωβιός, Numen. ap. Ath. 7.304e , 309c .
thighbone with the flesh on it, ham

Κωλιάς (sc. ἄκρα), άδος, ἡ, Colias, a promontory of Attica, Hdt. 8.96 ; with a temple of Aphrodite, St.Byz. : hence, as epith. of the goddess, Ar. Nu. 52 , Lys. 2 ; Κωλιάδες γυναῖκες Orac. ap. Hdt.l.c. (sc. γῆ), potter's clay of high repute, dug at Colias,…
κωλῡ-τήρ, ῆρος, ὁ, = κωλυτής, τῶν ἀδικούντων Archyt. 3 ; θεοὶ . . τῶν κακῶν κ. Porph. ap. Eus. PE 4.9 ; ἀριθμὸς κ. τῶν περαιτέρω ἐπιμορίων Iamb. in Nic. p.52 P.
κωλώτης, ου, ὁ, = ἀσκαλαβώτης , Arist. HA 609b19 , Babr. 204 , Hsch. ; epith. of Dionysus, Suid.

κῶνος, ου, masc., the fruit of the πεύκη, pine-cone, = στρόβιλος , Ps.- Hdt. Vit.Hom. 20 , Thphr. HP 3.9.5 , Theoc. 5.49 , Dsc. 1.69 , etc.; used in Orphic rites, Orph. Fr. 31.29 . edible seed of the πίτυς, Mnesith. ap. Ath. 2.57b ; πιτύϊνοι κ.…
λ, λάμβδα, or better λάβδα (v. sub voc.), τό, indecl., twelfth (later eleventh) letter of the Gr. alphabet: as numeral λ́ = 30 , but λ' = 30 , 000 .
the hollow on each side below the ribs, flank
λάζω, = λακτίζω, λάξας τράπεζαν Lyc. 137 , cf.Sch. E. Hec. 64 ; λάζειν: ἐξυβρίζειν, Hsch.

Λᾰκεδαίμ-ων, ονος, ἡ, voc. -ον v.l. in Pi. P. 10.1 :—Lacedaemon, the capital of Laconia, Od. 13.414 , etc.; also, Laconia itself, Il. 2.581 , Hdt. 1.67 , etc.: also as Adj., Διὸς Λακεδαίμονος Id. 6.56 ; Λ. γῆς E. Hel. 474 :—but regul. Adj. Λακεδαιμόνιος, α,…

Λᾰκων-ικός, ή, όν, Laconian, ἄνδρες Ar. Lys. 628 , etc.; κλειδίον, a kind of key, Id. Th. 423 , cf. Aristopho 7.4 , Men. 343 ; Λακωνικὸν πνέων Ar. Lys. 276 ; βραχυλογία τις Λ. Pl. Prt. 343b ; ἐλάττω ἔχειν γῆν τὸν ἀγρὸν ἐπιστολῆς Λακωνικῆς Prov.in Str. 1.2.30…
take hold of, lay hold on

ἄμφω, τώ, τά, τώ, also οἱ, αἱ , τά; gen. ἀμφοῖν S. Ph. 25 , etc., dat. ἀμφοῖν Aj. 1264 , etc.:—both, of individuals, Il. 1.363 ; of armies or nations, 2.124 :— Hom. uses only nom. and acc.: from Hom. downwards freq. with pl. Noun or Verb, Il. 2.767 , 7.255 ,…

λάπτω, fut. -ψω Il. 16.161 , (ἀπο-) Ar. Nu. 811 : aor. ἔλαψα Epic. Alex.Adesp. 1.10 , LXX Jd. 7.5 , (ἐξ-) Ar. Ach. 1229 : pf. λέλᾰφα Id. Fr. 598 :— Med. , fut. λάψομαι (ἐκ-) Id. Pax 885 : aor. ἐλαψάμην Pherecr. 95 :—lap with the tongue, of wolves, λάψοντες…
the great Nile perch, Perca (Lates) niloticus
modal Particle used with Verbs to indicate that the action is limited by circumstances or defined by conditions.

ἄν (B), [ᾱ], Att. , = ἐάν, ἤν , Th. 4.46 codd., al.; freq. in Pl. , ἂν σωφρονῇ Phd. 61b ; ἂν θεὸς θέλῃ ib. 80d , cf. D. 4.50 ; ἄν τ' . . ἄν τε Arist. Ath. 48.4 : not common in earlier Att. Inscrr., IG 1.2a5 , 2.179b49 , al.: but freq. later, SIG 1044.27…
ἄν (C) or ἀν, Epic form of ἀνά, q. v.
ἄν (D), shortened from ἄνα, v. sub ἀνά G.
ἅν, by crasis for ἃ ἄν, S. OT 281 , 580 , etc.
ἀν-, negat. Prefix, of which ἀ- privativum (q. v.) is a shortened form.
up, from bottom to top, up along
λάχ-η [ᾰ], ἡ, = λῆξις, ἀποκλήρωσις , Hsch. ; τάφων πατρῴων λάχαι (λαχαί codd.) ashare in their fathers' tombs, A. Th. 914 (lyr.).
ἄνα (B), ἡ, = ἄνυσις , Alcm. 23.83 , Call. Jov. 90 ; cf. ἄνη.
λάω (A) [ᾰ], = βλέπω, οὐδέ κεν αὐτὸν αἰετὸς ὀξὺ λάων ἐσκέψατο h.Merc. 360 ; γηθήσειε λάων is probably v.l. for γ. ἰδών in Il. 13.344 ( POxy. 769 ); cf. λάετε: σκοπεῖτε, βλέπετε, Hsch. , Cyr.
come to an end, turn out

ἀναβῐ-ώσκομαι, as Pass. , = ἀναβιόω (q. v.), Pl. Phd. 71e , al., Aristid. Or. 20(21).19 , Hierocl. in CA 26p.479M. : pf. inf. -βεβιῶσθαι Sannyr. 3 D. : aor. part. -βιωθεῖσα Philostr. V A 4.45 . causal of ἀναβιόω, bring back to life, ἀποκτεινύντων καὶ…

λευκ-άς, άδος, fem. of λευκός: Λ. πέτρη as pr.n. of mythical and real promontories, Od. 24.11 , Anacr. 19 , cf. E. Cyc. 166 ; Λ. alone, Th. 1.30 , etc. λ. ὀρεινή mountain deadnettle, Lamium maculatum, Dsc. 3.99 ; λ. ἥμερος dead-nettle, L. Moschatum, ibid.…

λεύσσω, by good authors used only in pres. and impf. (in codd. sts. with single ς, as also in IG (v.infr.), CIG 3284 (Smyrna), Hsch. ); Ep. impf. λεῦσσον Od. 8.200 ; Ion. λεύσσεσκον Emp. 129.5 : fut. λεύσω dub. in AP 15.7 , Man. 6.93 : aor. opt. λεύσσειε ib.…
λῆθος, Dor. λᾶθος, εος, τό, = λήθη , Theoc. 23.24 .
λῆσις (A), εως, ἡ , ̔λήθὠ = λῆστις , Hsch. s.v. ληθεδών (λύσις cod.); f.l. for λῆστις in Critias 6.12 D.
λῆσις (B), εως, ἡ , ̔λὦ = βούλησις, αἵρεσις , Hsch.
λίβα, λιβός, acc. and gen. of λίψ (q.v.).
the west bank of the Nile

ἀναγιγνώσκω, later ἀναγῑνώσκω: Ep. only in aor. 2 ἀνέγνων, know well, know certainly, οὐ γάρ πώ τις ἑὸν γόνον αὐτὸς ἀνέγνω Od. 1.216 , cf. 21.205 , Il. 13.734 . perceive, Theoc. 24.23 . know again, recognize, Od. 4.250 ; once in Hdt. , acknowledge, own,…
λίψ (C): ἐπιθυμία (cf. λίπτομαι), πέτρα ἀφ' ἧς ὕδωρ στάζει, Hsch.
put out to sea, set sail
λοχ-άζομαι, = λοχάω , Emp. 84.8 , AP 9.251 ( Even. ):— Act. in Hsch.
λῠάω, (λύη) = στασιάζω, ἀλλήλοις δ' ἐλύησαν Call. Aet.Oxy. 2080.76 , cf. Choerob. in Theod. 2.162 H.:— Med. , λυᾶται Hsch.
λύχνον, τό, = λύχνος , Hippon. 22 Diehl, BGU 338.1 , al. (ii/iii A. D.).
resolve a whole into its parts, dissolve, break up
λωφ-έω, lon. ( Ep. ) for foreg., A.R. 2.648 , 4.1627 , Nonn. D. 1.172 .

μ, μῦ, τό, Ion. μῶ Democr. 19 : indecl., thirteenth (later twelfth) letter of the Gr. alphabet: as numeral μ́ = 40 , but μ' = 40 , 000 .—In Inscrr. M stands for μύριοι or μυριάς: hence <*> for πεντακισμύριοι or πέντε μυριάδες, 50 , 000 .
μ', by elision for με; also for μοι, Ep. and Lyr., Il. 6.165 , al., Sapph. 2.13 , but rarely if ever in Trag., dub. in E. Med. 721 , IA 814 , S. Aj. 190 (lyr.).

μά (A) [ᾰ], Particle used in asseverations and oaths, c. acc. of the deity or thing appealed to; in itself neither affirmative nor negative, but made so by prefixing ναί or οὐ, or, in Att. , by the context: thus, ναὶ μὰ . . , in affirmation, ναὶ μὰ τόδε…
μά (B), Thess. for δέ, IG 9(2).258.11 (Cierium, ii B.C.), 461 A 9 (Crannon, ii B.C.); also found at beginning of sentence in POxy. 1216.10 (ii/iii A.D.).

μᾶ, shorter Aeol. and Dor. form for μάτηρ, in the phrase μᾶ γᾶ, = μῆτερ γῆ , A. Supp. 890 , 899 (both lyr.): as an exclam. used by women (perh. = Demeter), Herod. 1.85 , 4.20 ; μᾶ, πόθεν ὥνθρωπος; Theoc. 15.89 .
the act of learning, getting of knowledge

μᾰκᾰ́ρ-ιος, α, ον, also ος, ον Pl. Lg. 803c : collat. form. of μάκαρ, mostly used in Prose, but also in Poets, as Pi. , and freq. in E. , mostly of men, blessed, happy, Pi. P. 5.46 , E. Or. 86 , etc.; σοφοί τε καὶ μ. ἄνδρες Pl. R. 335e ; μ. τε καὶ εὐδαίμων…
μᾰ́κᾰρ-ος, α, ον, = μακάριος , Epigr.Gr. 454 (Trachonitis), 656 , dub. in IG 14.2258 (Lorium).

Μᾰκεδών, όνος, ὁ, ἡ, Macedonian, Hdt. 6.44 (pl.), etc.:—also Μακηδών (q. v.):—fem. Μακεδόνισσα, Stratt. 32 . Adj. Μακεδονικός, ή, όν, Hdt. 7.131 , etc.: -κόν (sc. φάρμακον), τό, Gal. 10.883 . Adv. - κῶς Arr. An. 7.12.2 , Plu. Cleom. 23 ; ἡ
μᾶλλον, Adv. Comp. of μάλα, v. μάλα 11 .
μάν, Dor. and old Ep. for μήν.
μᾱνίον, τό, Dim. of μάνης 1 , IG 11(2).287 B 138 , al. (Delos, iii B. C.), POxy. 1757.23 (ii A. D.).
μάομαι, v. μαίομαι . μᾰπέειν, Ep. aor. 2 inf. of μάρπτω (q.v.).

μᾰραίνω, fut. μᾰρᾰνῶ Orph. Fr. 262 , Epigr.Gr. 854 (Delos): aor.1 ἐμάρᾱνα h.Merc. 140 , S. OT 1328 , etc.:— Med. , aor. ἐμᾰρηνάμην (v. infr.):— Pass. , fut. μᾰρανθήσομαι Ep.Jac. 1.11 , Gal. 7.691 : aor. ἐμᾰράνθην Il. 9.212 , Lyc. 1231 , etc.: pf. μεμάρασμαι…
ἀνάζω, Tarent. for ἀνάσσω, Heraclid. ap. Eust. 1654.27 .

μάρτῠρος, ὁ, Ep. form for μάρτυς, ἐστὲ μάρτυροι Il. 2.302 , etc.; also in Central Greece, IG 9(1).226 (Drymaea), 364 (Naupactus), GDI 1684 , al. (Delph.), etc.: sg. once in Od. , οἷσιν ἄρα Ζεὺς μάρτυρος 16.423 , cf. PGen. 54.6 (iv A.D.). ( Zenod. rejected…
take the impression of, cling close to
hollow at base of a shoot, axil
mode of fighting, way of battle
Μεγιστώ, οῦς, ἡ, Greatness, personified, Emp. 123.2 .
free oneself from, let go one's hold of
μεῖον (A), ονος, τό, neut. of μείων (q.v.).
μεῖον (C), ου, τό, = μῆον , v.l. in Dsc. 1.3 , Androm. ap. Gal. 14.43 .
it is allotted, decreed by fate
μείρομαι (B), = ἱμείρομαι , c. gen., Nic. Th. 402 , Inscr.Perg. 203 .

μείς, μηνός, ὁ , nom. sg. μείς Il. 19.117 , Hes. Op. 557 , h.Merc. 11 , Anacr. 6.1 , Pi. N. 5.44 , Hdt. 2.82 , Hp. Septim. 3 (v.l.), Pl. Cra. 409c , Ti. 39c , Arist. GA 777b23 , Thphr. Sign. 27 , Call. Hec. 1.1.12 , SIG 1009 . 27 (Chalcedon, iii/ii B.C.),…

μεί-ων, so in Dor. , Leg.Gort. 9.48 , al., Schwyzer 323 B 9 (Delph., iv B. C.), Tab.Heracl. 1.114 ,al., Archyt. 1 , prob. in Epich. 62 (μηονος cod., and so in Diotog. ap. Stob. 4.7.62 , etc.), and Arc., IG 5(2).3.15 , 18 (Tegea): neut. pl. μείονα Hes. Op. 690…
μέλε (A), Ep. 3 sg. impf. from μέλω, Od. 5.6 .
μέλη, ἡ, a sort of cup, Anaxipp. 8 .

μελίζω (A), fut. -ιῶ LXX Le. 1.6 : aor. ἐμέλισα D.H. 7.72 : pf. Pass. μεμέλισμαι Opp. C. 3.159 : (μέλος A):—dismember, cutin pieces, Pherecyd. 32J. , D.H.l.c., Apollod. 1.9.12 . Pass. , have the limbs fully formed, Opp.l.c.
take up for oneself, take up, pick up
to be always going to do
to be an object of care
care for, take an interest in
to point out that the word or clause with which it stands is correlative to another word or clause that is to follow, the latter word or clause being introduced by δέ.
μέν used absolutely to express certainty, not followed by correlative δέ, indeed, of a truth
μέρα: ὄμματα, Hsch. μέρα, ἡ, = μέρος , PGrenf. 1.58.12 (vi A.D.).
care for, be anxious about, meditate upon
μέσον, τό, v. μέσος III and V.
in the midst of, among, between
in common, along with, by aid of
into the middle of, coming into
convey from one place to another, transfer
go by a different route, change one's course
give part of, give a share
raised from the ground, high in air
μεταρυσμόω (ῥυσμός Ion. , = ῥυθμός ), = μεταρρυθμόω, ἡ διδαχὴ μεταρυσμοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον Democr. 33 .
go to seek, go in quest of
ἀνακλάζω, aor. 2 ἀνέκλᾰγον E. IA 1062 , Call. Hec. 1.1.10 : aor. 1 ἀνέκλαγξα Ael. NA 12.33 :—cry aloud, scream out, E.l.c.; of a dog, bark, bay, X. Cyr. 1.4.15 ; of geese, cackle, Ael. l. c.
μετριόω or μετριάω, implied by the form μετριῶ (s.v.l.), Theognost. Can. 146 ; but ἐμετρίωμες, μετριώμεναι are forms of μετρέω (q.v.).
that by which anything is measured
not, the negative of the will and thought, as οὐ of fact and statement
not one, not even one, nobody
not at all, by no means
no more, no longer, no further
μήν, ὁ, v. μείς . Μήν, an Anatolian divinity, IG 22.1365 , 1366 , etc.; nom. sg. Μείς Supp.Epigr. 4.647.2 , 648.3 (Lydia).
μής, ὁ, v. μείς . μῆστο: ἐβουλεύσατο, Hsch. ; cf. μήδομαι.

μητίομαι, (μῆτις) Pi. P. 2.92 (s.v.l.): fut. -ίσομαι: aor. ἐμητισάμην: — = μητιάω 11 , devise, contrive, μητίσομαι ἔχθεα λυγρά Il. 3.416 ; τοσσάδε μέρμερ' ἐπ' ἤματι μητίσασθαι 10.48 ; μέγα ἔργον ἐμητίσαντο Od. 12.373 ; οἱ θάνατον μητίσομαι Il. 15.349 ;…

μήτῐς or μή τις, ὁ, ἡ, neut. μήτῐ, gen. μήτῐνος: (τὶς) old Gr. and Cret. for μηδείς, Il. 12.272 , al., Schwyzer 175 (Gortyn), Leg.Gort. 5.13 , al.; Cret. dat. sg. μηδιμί IG 22.1130.4 :—hence μήτι or μή τι, Adv., with imper., and inf. used imperatively, Il.…

μικκός, ά, όν, Dor. and Boeot. for μικρός, Ar. Ach. 909 , Archyt. 1 , Theoc. 5.66 , 8.64 , Call. Cer. 111 ; also (ή, όν) Ion. , αἱ μικκαὶ σφαῖραι Hp. Art. 3 (cod. Apollon.Cit. ); ἐλαίου μίκκον (sic) Id. Nat.Mul. 93 (v. l.), cf. 100 (v.l.), Call. Fr. 179 ,…
represent, express by means of imitation

Μίνως, [ῑ, but also ῐ Pl.Com. 15 D. ], ὁ, Minos, Hom. , etc.; gen. Μίνωος Od. 11.322 , 17.523 ; acc. Μίνωα Il. 13.450 , Od. 11.568 ; also gen. Μίνω Hdt. 1.173 ; acc. Μίνων Il. 14.322 , Hdt. 7.171 , Μίνω A. Ch. 618 (lyr.), Pl. Lg. 630d , A.R. 3.1107 ; dat.…

μισθαρν-έω, pf. μεμισθάρνηκα Aeschin. 1.154 :—work or serve for hire, ὅσοι μισθαρνοῦντες ἤνυσαν τάδε S. Ant. 302 , cf. Hp. Ep. 11 , Pl. R. 346b , D. 18.49 ; τῶν βαναύσων καὶ μισθαρνούντων Arist. Pol. 1296b29 ; οἱ μισθαρνοῦντες τῶν ῥητόρων Phld. Rh. 2.56 S. ;…
let out for hire, farm out
call to mind, remember, think of
to be remembered, had in memory
that which is meet and right
μολεῖν, aor. 2 inf. of βλώσκω (q. v.); hence a late pres. μολέω, Sch. Od. 17.219 , etc.

μόλῐς, Adv., post- Hom. synonym of μόγις, prevailing in Trag., Com., and Att. prose, though in Pl. and later prose μόγις was preferred (in A. the Laur. Ms. gives each form twice, the same Ms. of S. μόλις always); μ. μέν, ἀλλ' ὅμως ἠνεσχόμην Ar. Nu. 1363 , cf.…
μολυβδ-ώδης, ες, = μολυβδοειδής , Hp. Prog. 2 (interpol.), Dsc. 5.81 ; τὸ τῆς χροιᾶς μ. Gal. 11.282 .
monarchy, government by a single ruler
the only member of a kin
μονομᾰ́χ-ης, ου, ὁ, = μονομάχος , S.E. P. 1.156 .
ἀνάκωμα, ατος, τό, f.l. for ἀνακώναμα (?), [ Philol. ]ap. Stob. 1.20.2 .
Μόριος, ὁ, epith. of Zeus as guardian of μορίαι, S. OC 705 (lyr.).

Μοῦσα, ης, ἡ, Aeol. Μοῖσα Sapph. 84 , IG 42(1).130.16 , etc.; Dor. Μῶσα Alcm. 1 , etc.; Lacon. Μῶἁ (for Μῶσα) Ar. Lys. 1298 , cf. An. Ox. 1.277 :—Muse, Ὀλυμπιάδες Μ., Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο θυγατέρες Il. 2.491 , cf. Hes. Th. 25 , etc.; nine in number, first in Od.…
any art over which the Muses presided
to be trained in the ways of the Muses, to be educated
suffering hardship, in sore distress, wretched

μῦ, τό, name of the letter μ, IG 2.4321.24 (iv B. C.), Epigr. ap. Ath. 10.454f , Hellad. ap. Phot. Bibl. p.530 B. , etc. μῦ or μὺ μῦ, to represent a muttering sound made with the lips, μῦ λαλεῖν to mutter, Hippon. 80 (dub. l.); to imitate the sound of…
say over to oneself, con over, consider
μῦρος, ὁ, a kind of sea-eel, Dorio ap. Ath. 7.312f ; cf. σμῦρος.
μῶ, = ζητῶ , coined as etym. of many words, EM 84.47 , al. = μῦ 1 , Democr. 19 , BCH 29.483 (Delos, iii B. C.).
ν, νῦ, τό , indecl., fourteenth (later thirteenth) letter of Greek alphabet; as numeral, ν́ = 50 , but ν' = 50 , 000 .

ναίω, poet. Verb, Act. (intr.) only in pres. and impf. ( Ep. ναίεσκον Il. 5.708 ), fut. and aor. in causal and Med. and Pass. forms, v. infr. 11 , 111 : of persons, dwell, abide, mostly folld. by a Prep. of Place, ἐν Λ̔́ῃ, etc., Il.l.c., etc.; ῥοῇς ἔπι…
not done by fault, done unavoidably
anything flowing, running water, stream, spring
inmost part of a temple, shrine
νᾱός, Dor. and Att. poet. gen. from ναῦς. Νᾶος, v. Νάϊος .
one who rented and sub-let tenement-houses

νάω, only pres. and impf., Att. contr. νᾷ S. Fr. 5 , part. νῶντας Phot. :—flow, ἐν δὲ κρήνη νάει Od. 6.292 ; καὶ φρείατα μακρὰ νάουσιν Il. 21.197 ; ὄφρ' ἂν ὕδωρ τε νάῃ Epigr. ap. Pl. Phdr. 264d ; οἴνῳ Ἁχελῷος ἆρα νᾷ S.l.c.; ὕδατι νᾶε was running with . . ,…
νέα, Ion. acc. of ναῦς. v. νειός.
the lowest of the three strings
Νειλαιεύς, έως, ὁ, = sq., AP 9.353 ( Leon. Alex. ).
Νειλ-ῷος, α, ον, = Νειλαῖος , Luc. Nav. 15 , PMasp. 2 ii 21 (vi A.D.); τὰ Νειλῷα festival on the inundation of the Nile, Hld. 9.9 .
consider as part of purity, make it a point of religion

νέομαι, contr. νεῦμαι, Il. 18.136 : νείομαι v.l. in 23.76 ; 2 and 3 sg. contr. νεῖαι, νεῖται, Od. 11.114 , 14.152 , etc.; 1 pl. νεύμεθα Theoc. 18.56 , A.R. 2.1153 ; 2 pl. νέεσθε Id. 3.306 , νεῖσθε E. Alc. 737 ; imper. νεῖο AP 7.472b ( Leon. ); subj. 2 sg.…
νεώτατος, η, ον, Sup. of νέος.

νή, Particle of strong affirmation, with acc. of the divinity invoked, once in Trag., ν. τὼ Λαπέρσα, ν. τὸν Εὐρώταν τρίτον, ν. τοὺς ἐν Ἄργει καὶ κατὰ Σπάρτην θεούς S. Fr. 957 ; freq. in Com. and Prose, esp. in the phrase νὴ Δία, Ar. Eq. 319 , Th. 240 , etc.;…
νηλεής, ές, v. νηλής ; cf. ἀνηλεής.
νῆς, Adv., = ἔνης (v. ἔνος B), Hsch. : Dor. νᾶς (prob.), Id.

νῖκος, εος, τό, later form for νίκη, LXX 1 Es. 3.9 , BGU 1002.14 (i B.C.), IG 12 ( 5 ). 764.2 (Andros, prob. i A.D.; written νεῖκος), Ev.Matt. 12.20 , Vett.Val. 358.5 , Orph. A. 587 , APl. 5.381 , read by Aristarch. in Il. 12.276 ; εἰς νῖκος for ever, LXX 2…
that which is perceived, perception, thought
that which is in habitual practice, use

νος-ερός, ά, όν, = νοσηρός , of symptoms, Hp. Aph. 7.67 ; ν. κῶλον E. Or. 1016 (anap.); ν. κοίτα a bed of sickness, Id. Hipp. 131 (lyr.), cf. 179 (anap.); ν. χειμών Arist. Pr. 861b22 ; νοσερά, opp. ὑγιεινά, Polystr. p.3 W., cf. Alex.Aphr. in Top. 71.2 ;…
new moon : the first of the month
hollow between the under-lip and chin
ξάνθ-ωσις, εως, ἡ, = ξάνθισις , Ps.-Democr. Alch. p.54B.

ξέν-η, ἡ, fem. of ξένος : (sc. γυνή) foreign woman, A. Ag. 950 , etc. (sc. γῆ) foreign country, ἐν ξένᾳ S. Ph. 135 (lyr.); ἐπὶ ξένης X. Lac. 14.4 ; ἐπὶ ξ. καταβιοῦν Phld. Rh. 2.146S. , cf. Plu. 2.576c , etc.
go wrong, make a false step
surprise, astonish by some strange sight
to be a stranger, speak with a foreign accent
make one's friend and guest, entertain
rapidly moving to and fro, nimble
ἀναπεπταμένος, η, ον, pf. part. Pass. of ἀναπετάννυμι, q. v. Adv. -νως explicitly, Plot. 5.1.8 .
piece of wood, log, beam, post

Ο ο, sixteenth (later fifteenth) letter in Gr. alphabet : as numeral ό = 70 , but <*>o = 70 , 000 . The name of the letter was οὖ, Pl. Cra. 414c , al., Callias ap. Ath. 10.453d , Neoptol. ap. eund. 10.454f , AP 9.385 ( Steph. Gramm.) : this name was in…
ὅ, relat. Pron. masc. for ὅς, v. ὁ, ἡ , τό c. ὅ, neut. of relat. Pron. ὅς. ὂ ὂ ὂ, Interj., Ar. Th. 1191 .

ὄᾰρ-ος, ὁ,= ὀαριστύς, mostly in pl., Θέμιστι . . ὀάρους ὀαρίζει h.Hom. 23.3 ; ἐμοὺς ὀάρους καὶ μήτιας h.Ven. 249 ; παρθένιοι ὄ. Hes. Th. 205 ; ὄ. νυμφᾶν Call. Lav.Pall. 66 : generally, converse, discourse, Emp. 21.1 ; οἱ γὰρ ὄ. λόγοι εἰσί Pl. Min. 319e ;…
ὄγκος (C), ον, as Adj. ; v. ὀγκηρός fin.
ὀδμ-άομαι, ὀδμή, older forms of ὀσμάομαι, ὀσμή (q.v.).

ὁδοιπορ-έω, impf. ὡδοιπόρεον,-ουν, Hdt. 4.116 ( v.l. ὁ- ), S. OT 1027 : fut. -ήσω Hp. Art. 58 : pf. ὁδοιπόρηκα Philippid. 13 : plpf. 3 pl. διοδοιπορήκεσαν Hdt. 8.129 :— Pass. , pf. ὡδοιπόρηται Luc. Herm. 2 :— walk, Hdt. 4.110 , S. OT 801 ; ὀρθότεροι -ήσουσι…

ὀδῠν-άω, aor. ὀδυνῆσαι Gal. 10.853 :— Pass. , Phld. Lib. p.29 O. ; 2 sg. ὀδυνᾶσαι Ev.Luc. 16.25 : fut. ὀδυνηθήσομαι Gal. 10.851 , but ὀδυνήσομαι Men. 325.16 , Teles Fr. 2p.9H. : aor. ὠδυνήθην Ar. Ach. 3 :— cause one pain or suffering, τὸ γὰρ ὀρθοῦσθαι γνώμαν…

ὄζω, Dor. ὄσδω Theoc. 1.149 (cf. also III infr.): impf. ὦζε Crates Com. 2 (cj. Pors. for ὦ Ζεῦ): fut. ὀζήσω Ar. V. 1059 ; Ion. ὀζέσω Hp. Superf. 25 , Gp. 12.29.5 , Eust. 1523.39 , An.Ox. 2.396 : aor. ὤζησα Ar. Fr. 635 ; Ion. ὤζεσα Hp. Superf. 25 , LXX Ex.…
οι<>, enclit. οἱ, dat sg. of Pron. of 3 pers. masc. and fem. ; v. οὗ.
οἰάω, (οἶος) in part. οἰῶντα: μονάζοντα, Hsch.
οἴη (A), ἡ, = κώμη , GDI 5661.46 (Chios, iv B. C.), A.R. 2.139 , Hsch. , Theognost. Can. 18 ; cf. οἰήτης.

οἰκέτ-ης, ου, ὁ , ̔οἶκος̓ household slave, A. Ch. 737 , Hdt. 6.137 , 7.170 , Antipho 1.30 , Th. 2.4 ; δημόσιος οἰ. τῆς πόλεως Aeschin. 1.54 . οἱ οἰκέται also, = οἰκετεία , household, A. Ag. 732 (lyr.), Hdt. 8.4 , 106 , 142 , S. Tr. 908 , X. Cyr. 4.2.2 : hence…
practised in the management of a household
οἶμαι, shorter form of οἴομαι (q. v.).
οἶνον, τό, in pl., οἶνα: τὰ τῆς ἀμπέλου φύλλα, Hsch.
ἀνα-ποδόω, = ἀναποδίζω 11 , ἀ. ἐπὶ τὴν μονάδα Plu. 2.876f ἀναποδόομαι grow fresh feet, of scorpions, Lyd. Mag. 1.42 .
I think so, I should think so
single in its kind, unique, excellent
οἶσθα, οἶσθας, v. Εἴδω B. ὀϊσθείς, v. οἴομαι.
a sting, anything that drives mad
οἴω, Ep. ὀΐω, Lacon. οἰῶ, v. οἴομαι.
a large bird, bird of prey
ὅκκᾰ, Dor. Adv.,=ὅκα, ὅτε, Alcm. 94 , Cerc. 7.11 , Epigr.in Berl.Sitzb. 1894.908 . (From Ὁδ-κᾰ, cf. Lesb. ὄττι from Ὅδ-τι, etc.)

ὅκκᾱ, Dor. for ὅταν, Epich. 165 , al., Sophr. 46 , Ar. Ach. 762 (Megar.), IG 5(1).962.26 ( Lacon. ), 12(1).694.17 (Rhodes, iii B. C.), Archyt. Fr. 1 , Theoc. 1.87 , 4.21 . [ ὅκκᾱ Epich. 165 , Theoc. 8.68 , 11.22 (ὅκκ' Ar.l.c., ὅκχ' Epich. 29 , etc., v. κᾱ) :…
containing the first eight books of the Old Testament
ὁλάω, lisping pronunciation of ὁράω, Ar. V. 45 .
that which causes destruction, pest, plague
take a short time to rise
liable to be attracted, having a propensity
whole, entire, complete in all its parts
Ὀλυμπ-ίᾱσι, Adv., v. Ὀλυμπία, ἡ : but Ὀλυμπιάσι [ᾰ], dat. pl. of Ὀλυμπιάς.
to be in company with, consort with
hold converse with, be acquainted with, associate with

ἄγνῡμι, 3 dual ἄγνῠτον Hom. , v. infr.: fut. ἄξω (κατ-) Il. 8.403 : aor.1 ἔαξα Hom. , (κατ-) Ar. V. 1436 , etc., ἦξα Il. 23.392 , (κατ-) Hp. Epid. 5.26 ; imper. ἆξον Il. 6.306 ; part. ἄξας 16.371 , E. Hel. 1598 ( κατ-εάξαντες Lys. 3.42 codd., perh. to…
any assembled crowd, throng of people
eating at the same manger, messmates
ὁμο-κλής, ὁ, = ὁμόκλητος , poet. acc. ὁμοκλεα Id. Fr. 102 Bgk. (= 51b Schr.).
agree with, say the same thing as
ὁμο-μήτωρ, ορος, ὁ, ἡ, = foreg., Orph. Fr. 15 , Poll. 3.23 .
to be of one mind, agree
one and the same, common, joint
ὁμο-σίπῠος, ον , ̔σιπύἠ sharing the same meal-tub, messmate, Charond. ap. Arist. Pol. 1252b14 .

ὄνομαι, 2 sg. ὄνοσαι Od. 17.378 ; Ep. 2 pl. οὔνεσθε ( Aristarch. ὀνόσασθε, Buttm. and Pap. οὔνοσθε) Il. 24.241 ; 3 pl. ὄνονται Od. 21.427 , Hdt. 2.167 ; opt. ὄνοιτο Il. 13.287 : impf. 3 pl. ὤνοντο (κατ-) Hdt. 2.172 : Ep. fut. ὀνόσσομαι Il. 9.55 , Od. 5.379 :…
the ass as a beast of burden
(sum), the things which actually exist, the present
that which one has, property, fortune
without the teeth that tell the age

ὀπηδ-έω, Dor. ὀπᾱδέω (v. ὀπηδός), used by Hom. only in 3 sg. pres. ὀπηδεῖ, and impf. ὀπήδει (without augm.): inf. ὀπηδεῖν h.Ap. 530 :—follow, accompany, attend, τινι Il. 2.184 , 24.368 , Pi. P. 4.287 ; also ἅμα τινί Od. 7.165 , Hes. Th. 80 , h.Ap. l. c. ;…

ὁπλ-ίζω, aor. ὥπλισα, Ep. ὥπλισσα (v. infr.): pf. ὥπλικα (παρ-) D.S. 4.10 : plpf. ὡπλίκει D.C. 78.6 :— Med. , fut. -ίσομαι (ἐφ-) AP 9.39 ( Music. ), -ιοῦμαι Sch. Il. 13.20 : aor. ὡπλισάμην, Ep. ὁπλίσσατο ( v.l. ὡπλ- ) Od. 2.20 :— Pass. , aor. ὡπλίσθην Hdt.…

ὁπόθεν, Ep. ὁππόθεν, Ion. ὁκόθεν (never -θε, for ὁππόθ' Od. 3.89 is for ὁππόθι):—Adv. correl. to πόθεν : chiefly used in indirect questions, opp. ὅποι (q.v.), whence, from what place, εἴρεαι ὁππόθεν εἰμέν Od. 3.80 ; ἐρέσθαι, ὁππόθεν οὗτος ἀνήρ 1.406 , cf. Pi.…

ὅπου, Ion. ὅκου, Relat., indirect interrog., and indef. Adv. of Place, correlat. to ποῦ: as a Relat., sts. c. gen. loci, τῆς πόλεως ὅπου κάλλιστον στρατοπεδεύσασθαι Pl. R. 415d , cf. Hdt. 2.172 ; ὅπου βούλοιτο τοῦ δρόμου X. HG 2.4.27 ; ἔσθ' ὅπου in some…
ὁππόθεν, ὁππόθῐ, ὁπποῖος, Ep. for ὁπόθεν, ὁπόθι, ὁποῖος.

ὀπτάω, pf. ὤπτηκα Euphro 1.5 : irreg. part. Pass. ὀπτεύμενος Theoc. 7.55 : Dor. pres. part. ὀπτᾶντες Epich. 164 : fut. Med. ὀπτήσομαι (in pass. sense) Luc. Asin. 31 : aor. Pass. , ὀπτηθῆναι Od. 20.27 : pf. Pass. ὤπτημαι Ar. Fr. 627 : (ὀπτός (A), q. v.)…
in such a manner that, in order that.
any well-watered, fertile spot of land, meadow-land
to be getting ready to bear, growing ripe

ὀρέγω, Od. 17.366 , E. Ph. 1710 (lyr.), etc.; Ion. and later Prose, Hdt. 2.2 , Arist. HA 497b27 , etc.: impf. ὤρεγον Pi. P. 4.240 , App. BC 4.126 : fut. ὀρέξω Il. 13.327 , E. Med. 902 : aor. ὤρεξα Il. 23.406 , Trag. ( S. OC 846 , etc.), and sts. in Prose, Pl.…
ὀρές-της, ὁ, = ἐν ὄρεσι διαιτώμενος , Phot. : elsewh. only as pr. n. Ὀρέστης, voc. Ὀρέστα, S. El. 6 , 15 , etc.

ὀρεύς, Ion. οὐρεύς, έως , ὁ (even ὁ θῆλυς ὀ. Arist. HA 577b22 , though τῆς θηλείας follows τοῖς θήλεσιν ib. 573a16 ), mule, in Il. , as a beast of draught and burden, always in Ion. form, synon. with ἡμίονος, cf. 23.115 with 121 , and 24.702 with 716 ; also…
mark out by boundaries, mark out
the object by which one swears
ὁρμάζω, late form of ἁρμόζω, EM 631.49 , Aët. 16.26 ( v.l. ἁρμόζειν ).
set in motion, urge on, cheer on
to be moored, lie at anchor
rapid motion forwards, onrush, onset, assault
come to anchor, lie at anchor
made to rise up and depart, driven from one's house and home
which brought the birds of passage

ὄρνῡμι or ὀρνῑθ-ύω, poet. Verb: from the former come imper. ὄρνῠθι, ὄρνῠτε, Il. 6.363 , Od. 10.457 , al. ; inf. ὀρνύμεναι Il. 17.546 , ὀρνύμεν 9.353 , al.; and from the latter, pres. ὀρνύει Pi. O. 13.12 , cf. Orph. L. 222 : 3 sg. and pl. impf. ὤρνυε, -υον,…

ὀρούω, Pi. P. 10.61 , Democr. 228 : impf. ὤρουον E. HF 972 : fut. ὀρούσω h.Ap. 417 : aor. ὤρουσα Pi. O. 9.102 , A. Eu. 113 ; Ep. ὄρουσα Il. 2.310 , Hes. Sc. 437 , part. ὀρούσας Il. 11.359 , E. IT 297 : (cf. ὄρνυμι):— dart, rush forward, Hom. , both of men and…
ὀρφεύς, έως, ὁ, = ὀρφός, ὀρφώς , Marc.Sid. 33 (pl. ὀρφέες); with a pun on Orpheus, Alex. 113 .

ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (not ὅ, v. Il. 1.609 , 21.305 , Od. 11.515 ), gen. οἷο Il. 3.333 , Od. 1.330 , al., οὗ 23.150 , al. ; Cret. ϝός Leg.Gort. 1.18 ,al., SIG 1183 ; so in Aeol. , Sapph. Supp. 1.6 , Lyr.Adesp. 32 , cf. A.D. Pron. 107.11 :—POSSES S. PRON.: of the 3 pers.,…
the very man who, the very thing which
ὅσσα, Ion. and Ep. neut. pl. of ὅσος for ὅσα.
any one who, anything which, whosoever, whichsoever

ὀσφρ-αίνομαι, fut. ὀσφρήσομαι Ar. Pax 152 : aor. 2 ὠσφρόμην Hdt. (v. infr.), Ar. Ach. 179 ; inf. ὀσφρέσθαι Eup. 10 ; part. ὀσφρόμενος Philonid. 3 (the aor. 1 form ὤσφραντο in Hdt. 1.80 , Aristid. 2.308 J. seems to be an error of the copyists for ὤσφροντο…
ὅτε, neut. of ὅστε: also Ion. masc. for ὅστε, v. ὅς, ἥ, ὅ .
ὁτιοῦν, v. ὅστις iv. 2b . ὅτιπερ, v. ὅτι B. 1a . ὅτις, ὅτινα, ὅτινας, Ep. cases of ὅστις. ὀτίς, v. ὀτιαφόροι .
the negative of fact and statement, as μή of will and thought
also not, not . . either, nor yet
not either, neither of the two
no more, no longer, no further
certainly not, at any rate . . not
reaching to heaven, high as heaven
anything shaped like the vault of heaven
οὖρος (C), ὁ, Ion. , etc. for ὅρος (q. v.).
a material thing by which a connexion is established between the person to be acted upon and the supernatural agent
to such an extent, so, so much, so very, so excessively
οὐχ ὅπως, οὐχ ὅτι, v. ὅπως A. II. 2 , ὅτι A. v. οὐχί, Att. , v. οὐ fin.
to be bound, to be obliged
ὀφέλλω (A), Ep. , Aeol. , and Arc. for ὀφείλω (q. v. sub init.).
a surgical bandage covering one or both eyes
set up as a votive gift, dedicate
after a long time, at length, late
one who cooks food, a cook
ὄψος, εος, τό, = ὄψον , LXX Nu. 11.22 .
π, πεῖ, IG 22.2783.23 (iv B. C.), BCH 29.483 (Delos), Hellad. ap. Phot. p.530B. , indecl.: seventeenth (later sixteenth) letter of the Gr. alphabet: as numeral π́ = 80 , but π' = 80 , 000 .
πα, apoc. for παρά, πα Δάματρα, π. Δάματρι, GDI 3536a20 , 3542.11 (Cnidus).
all-in' contest in boxing and wrestling
πᾰλαιστ-ή, ἡ, = παλαστή (q. v.); Aeol. παλαίστα Alc. 33.6 ( v.l. παλάσταν ).
piece of handiwork, work of art
cause to give light, make to blaze up

Πάν, gen. Πᾱνός, dat. Πᾱνί (un contr. Πάονι IG 5(2).556 (Melpea, vi B. C.)), ὁ, Pan, Πᾶνα δέ μιν καλέεσκον, ὅτι φρένα πᾶσιν ἔτερψεν h.Hom. 19.47 , cf. 5 , Hdt. 2.145 , 6.105 , etc.; ὦ Πὰν Ἀρκαδίας μεδέων Pi. Fr. 95 , cf. Theoc. 1.123 , etc.; Π. κεροβάτας Ar.…

Πᾰνᾰθήναια (sc. ἱερά), τά, Panathenaea, festival at Athens, Hdt. 5.56 ; τὰ μεγάλα Π. Th. 5.47 , Lys. 21.1 , Isoc. 12.17 , IG 12.10.2 , 304.6 ; τὰ μικρὰ Π. Lys. 21.2 (also τὰ κατ' ἐνιαυτόν IG 22.334.32 ), cf. Ar. Nu. 988 , And. 1.28 , etc.; also at Ilium,…
Πᾰνᾰθήναιος, ὁ (sc. μήν), month at Ilium, Supp.Epigr. 4.663 .
visibly, openly, before the eyes of all
ἀναφαν-δόν, Adv. = foreg., Il. 16.178 , Hdt. 2.35 , 46 , Pl. Prt. 348e , etc.: poet. ἀμφανδόν Pi. P. 9.41 .
from all quarters, from every side
παντο-δᾰπής, ές, late form of -δαπός, Epicur. Herc. 1413.4 , Procl. in Prm. p.605 S., EM 204.23 , 711.48 .
of every kind, of all sorts, manifold
from all quarters, from every side
at all events, at any rate
look about one with a sharp, searching glance
from the side of, from beside, from
to one side of, by, past
to be in the same right ascension as
lead aside from the way, mislead
pass by, pass on one's way
give, hand over to another, transmit

παρα-δύομαι, Med. with intr. aor. Act. παρέδυν (v. infr.): pf. παραδέδῡκα Aeschin. 3.37 :—creep, slink, or steal past, ταῦτα δ' ἐγὼν αὐτὸς τεχνήσομαι . . , στεινωπῷ ἐν ὁδῷ παραδύμεναι Il. 23.416 ; ἐκδρᾶσα παρέδυν Ar. Ec. 55 . creep or steal in, ἐς τὰν ἀκοάν…

ἀναχάσκω, only pres. and impf., Ar. Av. 502 , Fr. 68 , Luc. VH 2.1 ; poet. ἄγχασκε Pherecr. 196 :—other tenses from pres. Ἀναχαίνω, fut. -χᾰνοῦμαι Hp. Superf. 29 : aor. 2 ἀνέχᾰνον: pf. ἀνακέχηνα:—open the mouth, gape wide, ἀναχανὼν μέγα Ar. Eq. 641 ; στόμα…

παραιν-έω, 3 sg. impf. παρῄνει Th. 1.139 ; Ion. παραίνεε Hdt. 8.19 : fut. -έσω S. OC 1181 , Ar. Pax 1245 , D. 37.11 , etc.; -έσομαι Pl. Mx. 236e : aor. παρῄνεσα S. Ph. 1434 , Ar. Ra. 1420 , Isoc. 12.264 ; Ion. -αίνεσα Hdt. 1.80 : pf. παρῄνεκα Isoc. Ep. 2.1 ,…

παράκειμαι, poet. πάρκειμαι Pi. (v. infr.): Ep. impf. παρεκέσκετο Od. 14.521 :—used as Pass. to παρατίθημι, lie beside or before, ἔτι καὶ παρέκειτο τράπεζα Il. 24.476 ; ὀϊστόν, ὅ οἱ παρέκειτο τραπέζῃ Od. 21.416 , cf. Pherecr. 108.17 , Telecl. 1.7 , etc.; ἡ…
take to oneself, associate with oneself
leave on one side, leave remaining
leave on one side, pass over
beside one another, side by side
to be changed and become salt

ἁνδάνω [δᾰ], impf. ἥνδανον, Ep. ἑήνδανον, in Ion. Prose ἑάνδανον Hdt. 9.5 and 19 (in 7.172 , 8.29 , codd. give ἥνδανον): fut. ἁδήσω Id. 5.39 : pf. ἅδηκα Hippon. 100 , Locr. ϝεϝάδηκα (v. infr. 11 ); ἕᾱδα A.R. 1.867 ; part. ἑαδώς Il. 9.173 : aor. ἑᾰδον Hdt.…
set one's seal beside another's, counterseal
set before oneself, have set before one

παρατρέπω, aor. 2 παρέτραπον Hes. Th. 103 :— Med. (v. infr.):— Pass. , aor. 2 παρετράπην App. Mith. 1 :—turn aside, off, or away, παρατρέψας ἔχε μώνυχας ἵππους ἐκτὸς ὁδοῦ Il. 23.423 , cf. 398 ; Ταντάλου λίθον παρά τις ἔτρεψεν ἄμμι θεός pushed it from our…

παραχωρ-έω, fut. -ήσομαι D. 23.105 , later -ήσω LXX 2 Ma. 8.11 :— go aside : rarely in lit. sense, to be displaced, Hp. Loc.Hom. 47 : mostly, make way, give place, abs., Ar. Ra. 767 , Ec. 633 , And. 1.26 , Pl. Smp. 213b , D. 17.1 , etc.; τινι for one, X. HG…
observe by the way, remark, notice
beside the main subject, subordinate, incidental
pass unnoticed, escape the notice of
Παρθένος at Chersonesus, IPE 12.352.49 (ii B. C.).
since it was in their power, since the opportunity offered
set by one's side, bring forward, produce
bring to one's side, bring over by force, bring to terms
παρόω, v. πηρόω . πάρπᾰγος, ὁ, = παράπαγος , Hsch.
fatherhood, descent from a common father
πε, reduced form (before initial τ) of πετ̔ἄ, = μετά , IG 5(2).6.98 (Tegea, iv B. C.), 262.16 (Mantinea, V B.C.).
mode of breaking in a horse by riding him in a figure-of-eight course
πέδιον, τό, Dim. of πέδη, EM 658.23 .
part of the foot next the toes, metatarsus
πεῖ, τό, name of the letter π, v. Π :—later πῖ, Sch.D.T. p.489 H., etc.
to be prevailed on, won over, persuaded
πειρήν, ῆνος, ὁ, a fish, Numen. ap. Ath. 7.306c .

πέλᾰγ-ος, εος, τό, gen. pl. πελαγέων Hdt. 4.85 , S. Aj. 702 (lyr.), πελαγῶν Th. 4.24 ; Ep. dat. πελάγεσσι (v. infr.) :—the sea, esp. high sea, open sea, π. μέγα Il. 14.16 , Od. 3.179 , etc.; ἐν πελάγεϊ ἀναπεπταμένῳ Hdt. 8.60 .ά ; διὰ πελάγους out at sea, opp.…

Πελασγός, ὁ, Pelasgian, Il. 2.843 , 17.288 : in pl. , 2.840 , 10.429 , Od. 19.177 , Hdt. 1.57 , etc. ; Δωδώνην Πελασγῶν ἕδρανον Hes. Fr. 212 ; used generally for Greeks, E. Or. 857 ; Τυρσηνοὶ Π. S. Fr. 270 (anap.) ; cf. πελαργός 11 .
πελάω, poet. form for πελάζω, 3 sg. πελάει Arat. 74 , Opp. C. 1.515 ; imper. πέλα Lyr.Adesp. 22 ; inf. πελάειν Opp. H. 5.496 , Ep. πελάαν h.Hom. 7.44 ; πελῶ is Att. fut. of πελάζω (q. v.).

πελειάς, άδος, ἡ, = foreg. 1 , mostly in pl. , Il. 11.634 , Hdt. 2.55 , A. Supp. 223 , E. Andr. 1140 , etc. ; τρήρωσι πελειάσιν . . ὁμοῖαι Il. 5.778 ; Ep. dat. πεληϊάδεσσι Opp. C. 1.351 : in sg. , Hdt. l. c., S. OC 1081 (lyr.) : distd. from περιστερά, Arist.…
like the head of a double axe
πελί-ωμα, ατος, τό, = πελίδνωμα , Hp. Coac. 394 , Acut.(Sp.) 2 , Arist. Pr. 891a1 , Thphr. HP 9.20.3 , Crito ap. Gal. 12.448 , BGU 928.13 , al. (iii A. D.).

πελώρ-ιος (also τελώριος (q. v.)), ον, fem. (not in Hom. ) -ιος Hes. Th. 179 , -ίη A.R. 4.1682 : = πέλωρος , freq. in Hom. , mostly of gods, Ἀΐδης, Ἄρης, Il. 5.395 , 7.208 ; or heroes, as Αἴας, Ἕκτωρ, Ἀχιλεύς, 3.229 , 11.820 , 21.527 ; Ὠρίων Od. 11.572 ; ἀνὴρ…
πέμπε, Aeol. , = πέντε , Ps.- Hdt. Vit.Hom. 37 ; gen. πέμπων Alc. 33.7 : πεμπεκαιδέκοτος, Aeol. for πεντεκαιδέκατος, IG 12(2).82.5 (Mytil.).
one who works for his living, day-labourer, poor
to be conscious, in full possession of one's faculties
bring to an end, finish, accomplish
*περάω (B), v. πέρνημι . περβέβαται, v. περιβαίνω III.
draw in outline, describe in general terms
one who goes the rounds, patrol
going round, marching round, flank march
going round in a circle, coming round to the starting-point, circuit
small bone of the arm, radius

Περσεφόνη, ἡ, Ep. Περσεφόνεια Il. and Od. , the common form first in h.Cer. 56 , Hes. Th. 913 ; Φερσεφόνη, Simon. 124 B. Pi. O. 14.21 , BMus.Inscr. 942 (iii B. C.), etc.; Φερσεφονείη, CIG 4588 ; Περσέφασσα, A. Ch. 490 , etc.; Φερσέφασσα, S. Ant. 894 , E. Hel.…

Περσικός, ή, όν, Persian, ἡ Περσική (sc. χώρα) Persia, Hdt. 4.39 , etc. Adv. - κῶς Ael. VH 12.1 . Περσικαί, αἱ , slippers, Ar. Nu. 151 ; τὼ Περσικά (dual) Id. Lys. 229 . ψιλὴ Π. Persian carpet, Callix. 2 . Περσικός, ὁ , or Περσικόν, τό , peach, v. μηλέα,…

Περς-ίς, ίδος, pecul. fem. of Περσικός, Persian, A. Pers. 59 (anap.), Th. 1.138 ; χώρη Hdt. 3.97 , al. as Subst., (sc. γῆ), Persis, Persia, Str. 15.3.1 , etc. (sc. γυνή) Persian woman, X. Cyr. 8.5.21 , etc. (sc. χλαῖνα) Persian cloak, Ar. V. 1137 .
by some way, to some place
πηγάς, άδος, ἡ, (πήγνυμι III) : = πάχνη , hoar-frost, rime, Hes. Op. 505 (pl.). (sc. γῆ) earth hardened after rain, Hsch.
πήγνῡσις, εως, ἡ, = πῆξις , Ps.-Thales ap. Gal. 16.37 .

πημ-αίνω, Il. 15.42 : fut. - ᾰνῶ S. Aj. 1314 , OC 837 ; Ion. -ανέω Il. 24.781 : aor. ἐπήμηνα 3.299 , S. Tr. 715 , Pl. R. 364c ; Dor. part. πημάνας [ᾱ] IG 12.1085.8 :— Med. , fut. πημᾰνοῦμαι Ar. Ach. 842 (s. v.l.), also πημανούμενος in pass. sense, S. Aj. 1155…

πήσσω, Att. πήττω, later form for πήγνυμι, LXX Si. 14.24 , Ph. 1.420 , Dsc. 4.188 , Arr. Epict. 1.19.4 , S.E. M. 9.247 , (κατα-) Str. 4.3.5 , D.H. 3.22 : impf. ἔπησσον Satyr. 1 :— Pass. πήττομαι Antig. Mir. 174 , Str. 13.4.14 , 7.3.18 (συμ-).
πικρ-άς, άδος, ἡ, = ἀνδρόσακες , Ps.- Dsc. 3.133 .
to be filled, be full of
πῖος, α, ον, poet. form of πίων, ἄρνες Epich. 136 ; μῆλα Orph. A. 506 : hence πῑότερος, πῑότατος, v. πίων .

πῐπίσκω, Hp. Mul. 1.63 , Luc. Lex. 20 : fut. πίσω [ῑ] Pi. I. 6(5).74 , Eup. 115 : aor. ἔπῑσα Hp. Mul. 1.59 , al., prob. in Arist. EN 1111a14 (for παίσας), (ἐν-) Pi. Fr. 111 (πιπίσαι is f.l. in Hp. Fract. 36 ):— Med. , aor. ἐπῑσάμην (ἐν-) Nic. Th. 573 , 877 ,…
trust, put faith in, rely on
that which is entrusted, a trust
to be made trustworthy, give a pledge
give mutual pledges of fidelity, exchange troth
πλάδ-η [ᾰ], ἡ, = πλάδος , Emp. 75 , Suid. s.v. πλαδαρόν (pl.).

πλᾰν-ήτης, ου, Dor. πλανάτας, ὁ, = πλάνης 1.1 , S. OC 3 , 124 (lyr.), E. Ba. 148 (lyr.), etc.; τοὺς π. ἐπὶ τὰς πόλεις ἐμπόρους [καλοῦμεν] Pl. R. 371d ; πλανῆται ἐπὶ πάντας τόπους, of hares, X. Cyn. 5.17 . as Adj., π. ἄθλιος βίος E. Heracl. 878 , cf. Porph.…
πλάτος (B) [ᾰ], ὁ, = πλάτας , IGRom. 4.866 (Laodicea ad Lycum).
πλέον, = πλήν , c. nom., JHS 50.267 (Asia Minor).

πλέω, Ep. πλείω Od. 15.34 , 16.368 : Ep. impf. ἀπ-έπλειον 8.501 : also Ep. and Ion. πλώω (v. infr.): Att. contr. imper. πλεῖ E. Tr. 102 (anap.): fut. πλεύσομαι Od. 12.25 , Il. 11.22 (ἀνα-), Hdt. 2.29 , Th. 6.104 , etc.; later πλευσοῦμαι SIG 402.27 (Chios, iii…
πλέων, neut. πλέον, pl.πλέω; v. πλείων.
πληγ-άς, άδος, ἡ, = δρέπανον , Id. Πληγάδες, αἱ, = Συμπληγάδες , A.R. 2.596 , 645 .

πληθ-ύς, ύος, ἡ, Ep. dat. πληθυῖ Il. 22.458 , Od. 11.514 , 16.105 :— Ion. for πλῆθος, throng, crowd, of people, Hom.ll. cc.; = δῆμος , Leg.Gort. 6.52 ; majority, πληθὺν δὲ νικῆν IG 9(1).333.18 ( Locr. , v B.C.): as Noun of multitude with pl. Verb, ὣς φάσαν ἡ…
receive a blow, to be heavily defeated
πλούσιον: θαλασσιοειδές, οἱ δὲ τὸ ὕδωρ, Hsch.

πλουτ-ίζω, Att. fut. -ιῶ Timocl. 4.8 :— make wealthy, enrich, τινα A. Ag. 586 , X. Cyr. 8.2.22 ; ἀρετῇ τινας Id. Mem. 4.2.9 ; τὴν πατρίδα IGRom. 3.199 (Ancyra): iron., π. τινὰ ἄτης (ἄτην codd.) A. Ag. 1268 :— Pass. , Ἅιδης στεναγμοῖς καὶ γόοις π. S. OT 30 ;…
πλοῦτος, εος, τό, = πλοῦτος, ὁ, 2 Ep.Cor. 8.2 , v.l. in Ep.Rom. 9.23 , Ep.Col. 1.27 , 2.2 .
of the nature of breath, whispered
ποδὸς ῥυτίς: τὸ τῶν ποδῶν ἕλκεσθαι, Hsch. (Fort. ποδορρυτί.)
work in various colours, work in embroidery

ποιπνύω, impf. ἐποίπνυον, Ep. ποίπνυον Il. 24.475 : aor. part. ποιπνύσας 8.219 . [υ of pres. long before a long syll., short before a short syll., v. infr.: ῡ in fut. and aor. always.]:— Ep. Verb (perh. formed by redupl. from πνῡ-, cf. πέπνυμαι), bustle…
make hostile, make an enemy of
πόλεων, gen. pl. of πόλις:—but πολέων, Ion. gen. pl. of πολύς.
condition and rights of a citizen, citizenship
civil polity, constitution of a state
have a certain form of government
belonging to, connected with one's city
having relation to public life, political, public
suited to a citizen's common life, ordinary
from many considerations, for many reasons
πολυ-μνήστη, ἡ, (μνάομαι) = foreg., Od. 4.770 , 14.64 , 23.149 :—later in form πολύ-μνηστος, κούρη Nonn. D. 42.497 ; πολυμνάστοιο . . Τίσιδος AP 6.274 ( Pers. ).

πολυπραγμ-ονέω, Ion. πολυπρηγμ-, pf. πεπολυπραγμόνηκα Phld. Sign. 33 :—to be busy about many things, μὴ πολυπραγμόνει take no trouble about it, Pherecr. 154 ; π. τὰς αἰτίας ἐρευνῶντας Pl. Lg. 821a ; περί τι ib. 952d ; περί τινα Phld. Ind.Sto. 22 ; ὑπὲρ σοῦ…
at a high price, very costly
subject to many forms of destruction
πόμα, τό, v. πῶμα. = φοῖνιξ , cj. in Dsc. 1.109 .
who escorted the souls of the dead
to be in a bad state
in bad case, in sorry plight, useless, good-for-nothing
anything produced by work, a work

πόντος, ὁ: Ep. gen. ἐκ ποντόφιν Od. 24.83 :—sea, esp. open sea, common from Hom. downwds., exc. in Prose, where it is chiefly used of special seas (v. infr. 11 ); in the general sense, ὁπότε πνεῦμα ἐκ πόντου εἴη Th. 4.26 , cf. Pl. R. 611e , Ti. 25a , LXX Ex.…

πόποι, exclam. of surprise, anger, or pain, ὢ π. freq. in Hom. , always at the beginning of a verse and sentence; ὢ π., οἷον ἔειπε . . Od. 17.248 ; ὢ π., οἷον δή νυ . . 1.32 ; ὢ π., ὡς . . 10.38 , al; ὢ π., ἦ μάλα . . Il. 16.745 , al.; ὢ π. οὐδέ νύ σοί περ…
hold up what is one's own
hold on by one another, hang together
means of passing a river, ford, ferry

πορφυρ-έω, ͂ πορφύρω, ἁλὶ πορφυρεούσῃ v.l. in Arat. 158 ; ἀμέθυστον . . πορφυρέουσαν ( v.l. πορφύρουσαν ) D.P. 1122 ; χρυσῷ πορφυρέοντι Opp. C. 2.597 (vv.ll.πορφύρεον, πορφυρόεντι; πορφύροντι cj.Schneider); λειμῶνες ἀνήροτα πορφυρέουσι v.l. for -φύρουσι ib.…
ἀνέω [ᾱ], = πτίσσω , Ar. Fr. 694 ( v.l. αἰνεῖθ' ), Ath. 10.4553 , Paus. Gr. Fr. 21 , prob. in Poll. 7.24 (ἀλεῖν codd.). Cf. αἵνω, ἀφᾱνέω.

*πόρω, assumed as pres. to aor. Act. ἔπορον and pf. Pass. πέπρωμαι: no example occurs of fut. πορῶ, Aeol. πόρσω, cited by EM 683.54 : aor. ἔπορον, Hom. mostly without augm.; part. πορών Il. 21.80 , Od. 19.460 , A. Pr. 946 ; inf. πορεῖν S. OT 1255 :—furnish,…

Ποσειδῶν (perispom. in Att. , Hdn.Gr. 2.914 ), ὁ; gen. ῶνος, also ῶ Aristias 1 ; acc. Ποσειδῶ Ar. Lys. 1165 , IG 22.111.67 ; voc. Πόσειδον S. Fr. 371.1 (lyr.), Ar. Ra. 664 : contr. (first in Hes. Th. 732 (s.v.l.)) from Ep. form (also used by Pi. P. 4.204 ,…

πόσις, ὁ, poet. πόσσις AP 6.323 ( Leon. ); gen. πόσιος (no gen. is found in Att. , πόσεως only in Hdn.Gr. 2.700 ); dat. πὁσει, Ep. πόσεϊ Il. 5.71 ; voc. πόσι E. Alc. 323 , Ar. Th. 913 ; also πόσις E. Hel. 1399 : pl. πόσεις Id. IA 176 (lyr.); acc. πόσιας Il.…
not yet come to man's estate
one of other, either of the two
that which befalls one, lot, destiny

πότνια, ἡ, poet.title of honour, used chiefly in addressing females, whether goddesses or women: as Subst., = δέσποινα (cf. Apion ap. Apollon. Lex. ), mistress, queen (v. sub fin.), πότνιαν ἁγνήν h.Cer. 203 : mostly c. gen., πότνια θηρῶν (nom.) queen of wild…
take in hand, treat laboriously, be engaged in
exaction of money, recovery of debts, arrears

πρᾰπίδες, αἱ, dat. πραπίσιν Pi. O. 2.94 , Ep. πραπίδεσσι (v. infr.):— poet., = φρένες , midriff, diaphragm, βάλε . . ἦπαρ ὑπὸ πραπίδων Il. 11.579 , cf. 13.412 , 17.349 : then, since this was deemed the seat of mental powers and affections, understanding,…
πρᾶτος, α, ον, Dor. for πρῶτος, Epich. 88 , al., IG 42(1).40.11 (Epid., v/iv B. C.), etc.: Sup. πράτιστος Theoc. 1.77 , IG 12(3).436 , 540 (Thera), Berl.Sitzb. 1927.161 (Cyrene).
πρέπων, οντος, ὁ, a sea-fish, Opp. H. 1.146 , Ael. NA 9.38 .

πρεσβ-ύτης [ῡ], ου, ὁ, prose form of πρέσβυς 1 , Hp. Aër. 10 (pl.), Th. 3.67 (pl.), Arist. EN 1157b14 (pl.), etc.; the sixth of the seven ages, Hp. Hebd. 5 ; also in Trag. and Com., E. Ph. 847 , Ar. Eq. 525 , Nu. 358 ; πατέρα π. Κρόνον A. Eu. 641 ; ἀνὴρ π.…
veins of the neck when swollen by anger

προαιρ-έω, fut. -ήσω Babr. 108.26 : aor. προεῖλον:—bring forth, produce from one's stores, προαιρούσαις λαθεῖν (prob. l.) ἄλφιτον, ἔλαιον κτλ. Ar. Th. 419 ; ἰσχάδας Pherecr. 68 ; τὸν σῖτον . . ἐντεῦθεν προαιροῦντας πωλεῖν Th. 8.90 ; ἐκ τοῦ ταμιείου Thphr.…
to have the chief voice in counsel
make up one's mind beforehand, prejudge
child by a former marriage, step-son
take legal proceedings, appear in court
to be the first, have the start

προθῡμ-έομαι, impf. προὐθυμούμην Th. 4.12 , Pl. R. 402b ; in Hdt. προεθ- (with v.l. προθ- ), 5.78 , 9.38 , also in X. Ages.. 2.1 , Pl. Cra. 395d : fut. προθυμήσομαι X. Cyr. 2.3.3 , Pl. Men. 74b , Plt. 262a ; προθυμηθήσομαι v.l. in Lys. 25.17 and Pl. Phd. 115c…
as a free gift, freely, at one's own cost
lie before, lie in front of
on the side of, in the direction of
that which is put upon a weapon

προσδοκ-άω, Ion. προσδοκ-έω (which is sts. found as f.l., e.g. in Plb. 23.7.3 ): fut. -ήσω: aor. -εδόκησα: pf. προσδεδόκηκα Memn. 45.3 :—expect, whether in hope or fear; mostly c. inf. fut., expect that one will do or that a thing will be, A. Pr. 930 , 988 ,…
living in the fields, wild, savage.
ἀνθρωπώ, ἡ, Lacon. for ἄνθρωπος 11 , Hsch.
to have come, be at hand, be present
πρόσθε, Ion. and poet. for πρόσθεν (q.v.).
πρόσθη, ἡ,= πρόσθεσις, dub. in Hsch. (fort. προσθή<κη>).
to be assigned to, fall to, belong to
cause to lean against, place against

ἀνιάω [ᾰν], S. Aj. 266 , etc.: 3 sg. impf. ἠνία ib. 273 , Pl. Grg. 502a : fut. ἀνιάσω [ᾱς] X. An. 3.3.19 , Ep. ἀνιήσω Hom. : aor. ἠνίᾱσα And. 1.50 , etc.; Dor. ἀνίᾱσα Theoc. 2.23 : pf. ἠνίᾱκα Hld. 7.22 :— Pass. , ἀνιῶμαι Od. 15.335 , etc., Ion. 3 pl. opt.…
one who stands before, front-rank man
one who stands before and protects, guardian, champion
gift of interpreting the will of the gods, gift of prophecy
one who speaks for a god and interprets his will
πρόχειρ-ον, τό,= προχείριον, Stud.Pal. 20.67.39 (ii/iii A.D.). crutch used in moving and flattening wool in the dyebath, PHolm. 26.2 , 5 .
make to stand up, raise up
rise to go, set out, go away
πρῶτος, η, ον, v. πρότερος B.
Πτολεμ-αῖος, ὁ, Ptolemy, name of the Kings of Egypt in the period after Alexander: also of a month at Methymna, dub. in IG 12 ( 2 ). 500 .
Πῡθᾰγόρ-ας, ου, Ion. Πῡθᾰγόρ-ης, εω, ὁ, Pythagoras, Hdt. 4.95 , etc.

Πῡθᾰγορ-ικός, ή, όν, = Πυθαγόρειος, μῦθοι Arist. de An. 407b22 ; βαθύτης Hierocl. in CA 26p.480M. ; τὰ Π., title of work by Zeno the Stoic, D.L. 7.4 . Adv. -κῶς in the Pythagorean manner, Plu. 2.728e , Iamb. Comm.Math. 22 : Comp. -κώτερον S.E. M. 4.11 , Iamb.…

Πῡθώ, gen. οῦς, dat. οῖ, ἡ, Pytho, the region in which lay the city of Delphi, Πυθοῖ ἔνι πετρηέσσῃ Il. 9.405 ; Π. ἐν ἠγαθέῃ Od. 8.80 , Hes. Th. 499 , etc.; of Delphi itself, Pi. P. 4.66 , 10.4 , Hdt. 1.54 , etc. (Acc. to the legend, derived from the rotting…
πυκνά, neut. used as Adv., v. πυκνός B. 11 .
to be open, stand open, lie open
one wing of a pair of double gates

πυνθάνομαι, Od. 2.315 , etc.; poet. also πεύθομαι (q.v.): Ep. impf. πυνθανόμην 13.256 : fut. πεύσομαι Il. 18.19 , etc., Dor. πευσοῦμαι Theoc. 3.51 (so cod. Med. in A. Pr. 988 ): aor. ἐπῠθόμην Il. 5 . 702 , etc., Ep. and Lyr. πυθόμην Od. 4.732 , B. 15.26 ;…
part of an army drawn up in close order, column
πῠρετ-έω,= foreg., dub. in PGurob 5.6 (iii B.C.).
πῠρή, ῆς, ἡ, Ion. and Ep. for πυρά. πῠρήϊον, τό, Ion. for πυρεῖον.

πωλέομαι, Ion. πωλεῦμαι, used by Hom. in 2 sg. πώλεαι Od. 4.811 ; part. πωλεύμενος 2.55 (also in A. Pr. 645 ): impf. πωλεύμην Od. 22.352 , πωλεῖτο 9.189 ; Ion. impf. πωλέσκετο Il. 1.490 , Od. 11.240 : fut. πωλήσομαι h.Ap. 329 , Ep. 2 sg. πωλήσεαι Il. 5.350 :—…
πωμ-ᾰτίζω,= πωμάζω, Gal. UP 4.8 ( Pass. ), 14.291 , v.l. in Dsc. 2.76.9 ( Pass. ).
πώποκα, Dor. for sq., οὐ πώποκα Epich. 1701 .
in any way, at all, by any means

Ρ ρ, ῥῶ, τό, indecl., twentieth (later seventeenth) letter of the Gr. alphabet: as numeral ρ́ = 100 , but ρ' = 100 , 000 : reckoned as a semivowel by Arist. Po. 1456b28 : the name ῥῶ occurs in Ar. Th. 781 , Callias ap. Ath. 10.453d , Pl. Cra. 426c , BCH…
ῥαίδ-ιον, τό, Dim. of foreg., Gloss.; written ῥέδιον in Hsch.
strike with a stick, cudgel, thrash
the lower part of the back, the chine
portion of an Epic poem fit for recitation at one time

Ῥέᾱ, ἡ, Ep. Ῥείη Il. 14.203 (in gen. Ῥείης, v.l. Ῥείας ), h.Cer. 442 , h.Ap. 93 (Ῥέη codd.), h.Ven. 43 , Hes. Th. 625 (Ῥείαν ib. 135 ); Ῥεῖα δ' ὑποδμηθεῖσα ib. 453 (but with v.l. Ῥείη δ' αὖ δμηθεῖσα ); gen. Ῥείας AP 6.219.20 (Antip.); the common form Ῥέα is…
ῥέον, οντος, τό , ̔ῥέὠ = ῥυτόν ( ῥυτός 11 ), Astyd. 3.3 .
ῥέον, τό, = ῥῆον , Aët. 1.347 , Alex.Trall. 5.5 , 9.2 , 12 , Paul.Aeg. 7.11.59 .
in a state of flux, flowing

ῥηγ-μίν or ῥηγ-μίς (neither form is found, unless [ῥηγμὶ]ν is to be restd. in IGRom. 4.272.1 (Elaea, cf. Wiener Sitzb. 214(4).26 )), gen.ῖνος, ἡ, sea breaking on the beach, surf (v. ῥήγνυμι B. 1 ), ἄκρον ἐπὶ ῥηγμῖνος ἁλὸς . . θέεσκον Il. 20.229 ; κώπῃσιν ἁλὸς…

ῥιγ-όω, fut. -ώσω X. Mem. 2.1.17 , Ep. inf. -ωσέμεν Od. 14.481 : aor. ἐρρίγωσα Hp. Epid. 3.1 .ς́, (ἐν-) Ar. Pl. 846 : pf. ἐρριγωκότες Thphr. Ign. 74 (vv. ll. ἐρριγότες, ἐρριγνωκότες), Gal. 11.556 .—Like ἱδρόω, has an irreg. contr. into ω , ῳ, for ου, οι, 3…
that from which anything springs as from a root
ῥῑνόν, τό,= ῥινός 11.1 , hide, Il. 10.155 , AP 9.328 ( Damostr. ). = ῥινός 11.2 , shield, Od. 5.281 , v. Sch.
ῥόον, τό, only in pl. ῥόα,= τὰ ἐκ τῆς συκαμίνου μόρα τὰ ἄωρα ξηρανθέντα, Hp. ap. Gal. 19.135 : but in sg., ὁ
that which is supped up, thick gruel

ς', by apostr. for δέ; also, though rarely, for σοί; v. σύ . for σά, but in Hom. only in phrases τὰ ς' αὐτοῦ, τὰ ς' αὐτῆς, Od. 14.185 , Il. 6.490 , al.; so, in Trag. and later Poets, τὰ ς' S. OT 329 , 405 , Ph. 339 , El. 1499 , E. Supp. 456 .
σάκος [ᾰ], ὁ , v. σάκκος . σᾱκός, ὁ, v. σηκός .
σᾱμεῖον, τό, Dor. for σημεῖον, Archyt. 1 .

Σάμος [ᾰ], ἡ , Samos, the name of several Greek islands: old name for Κεφαλληνία (q.v.), Il. 2.634 , Od. 4.671 ; also called Σάμη, 1.246 , h.Ap. 429 ; though this, acc. to others, is a town on the island: hence Adj. Σαμαῖος, α, ον, Str. 10.2.13 . Σάμος…
suiting a Satyr, like a Satyr

σελην-αίη, ἡ, Ion. and Ep. for σελήνη, Emp. 43 , Ar. Nu. 614 , A.R. 1.500 , IG 14.1389 i 27 , etc., and in later Prose, Luc. Astr. 3 , 17 ; prov., ἡ Ἀκέσεω ς. 'the Greek Kalends', Herod. 3.61 ; Dor. σελᾱναία E. Ph. 176 (lyr.), Pl. Cra. 409c .
Selene, the goddess of the moon
Σ. earth used in adulterating indigo, Dsc. 5.155 , Plin. HN 35.46 , 194 .
σεμέλη: τράπεζα, παρὰ δὲ Φρυνίχῳ ( Phryn.Trag. 23 ) ἑορτή, Hsch.
σεῦτλον, τό, Ion. and Hellenistic for τεῦτλον (q.v.).
to be put in quick motion
show by a sign, indicate, point out
the process by which the intestines reject that part of food which is not nutritious
anything made of iron, iron tool

Σῐκελ-ία, Ion. -ιη, ἡ, Sicily, Pi. P. 1.19 , al., Hdt. 1.24 , etc.: hence Σῐκελίδης, ου, ὁ, Dor. Σικελίδας, name given by Theoc. ( 7.40 ) to Asclepiades, and variously expld. in Sch.ad loc. [Σῑ- in dactylics, as ἄρχετε Σῑκελικαί . . , Mosch. 3.8 , etc.;…
tented cover, tilt of a wagon

σκῆψις, εως, ἡ, ( σκήπτω 1.2 ) pretext, plea, excuse, τοιάδε μέντοι ς. οὐ δόλον φέρει A. Ag. 886 ; μὴ ς. οὐκ οὖσαν τίθης S. El. 584 : c. gen., κατὰ φόνου τινὰ ς. pleading some murder as an excuse, Hdt. 1.147 ; ς. τοῦ μὴ τὰ δέοντα ποιεῖν a plea, excuse for not…
an uninvited guest, introduced by another

σκοπ-έω, used by early writers only in pres. and impf. Act. and Med. (v. infr. 11 ), the other tenses being supplied by σκέπτομαι (q.v.):—but in later writers we find fut. σκοπήσω, Anon. Prog. in Rh. 1.615 W., Gal. UP 3.10 (f.l.), (ἐπι-) Babr. 103.8 , (κατα-)…
one that watches, one that looks about

σκόρδ-ον, τό, = σκόροδον , Crates Theb. 4.5 D., IG 22.1184.15 (iv B.C.), PSI 4.332.6 (iii B.C.), PTeb. 717.5 (ii B.C.), LXX Nu. 11.5 , Phld. Po. 2.52 , Dsc. 2.152 , IG 3.73.10 , Edict.Diocl. 6.23 , Gp. 12.8.8 , etc.: prov., μὴ σκόρδου (sc. φάγω) 'anything for…
σκορπίον, τό,= τράγος (the plant), Dsc. 4.51 . = σίκυς ἄγριος , Ps.- Dsc. 4.150 . = heliotropium (i.e. σκορπιοκτόνον), Gloss.
in the dark, in secret, secret
come opposite to, meet face to face, meet with
σκῡτ-εύς, έως, ὁ,= σκυτοτόμος, Ar. Av. 491 , Pl. Grg. 491a , X. Ages. 1.26 , Archipp. 30 , PPetr. 2p.108 (iii B.C.), etc.
σοί, v. σύ . σοιδηύδεις: βάκχαι . . , Hsch. σοίθης: ψίθυρος, ἀλαζών, διάβολος, Id. σοίκιδες: κώνωπες, Id. σοῖο, Ion. gen. of σός, σόν.
σοῦ, gen. of σύ; also of σός. (In Hom. only the latter.)
master of one's craft, adept, expert
σπᾰν-ία, ἡ,= σπάνις, E. Rh. 245 (lyr.), D.S. 24.1 , Phot.

σπέρχω, Il. 13.334 , etc. ( Act. only in pres. and impf.):— Med. , fut. σπέρξομαι, aor. ἐσπερξάμην, Hsch. :— Pass. , Il. 19.317 , etc.: aor. part. σπερχθείς Pi. N. 1.40 , Hdt. 1.32 :—poet. Verb (used also in Ion. Prose, cf. περισπέρχω; Att. only in compds.…
one who runs in the stadium, one who runs for a prize
the line which bounds the racecourse, goal
brought to a stand, standing, stationary
party formed for seditious purposes, faction
covering so as to keep out water, water-tight
cover closely, so as to keep

στείχω, Il. 2.287 , Alc. 19 , A. Th. 467 , etc.; also στίχω, Hdt. 3.14 , Hsch. ; subj. στίχῃ Hdt. 1.9 ( v.l. στείχῃ ): Ep. impf. στεῖχον Il. 9.86 , etc.: aor. 1 ἔστειξα (only in compd. περίστειξας Od. 4.277 ): aor. 2 ἔστῐχον Il. 16.258 , Call. Del. 153 ,…
to be fond of, show affection for
στερόπ-ης, ου, ὁ, Lightner, name of one of the three Cyclopes, Hes. Th. 140 , Call. Dian. 68 .
to be put round in a circle
the breast as the seat of feeling and thought
the shadow of the gnomon, the length of which in feet indicated the time of day
a line of poles supporting hunting-nets
turn about with oneself, take back
stand firm, resist pressure, offer resistance
στροβῑ́λ-ιον, τό, Dim. of στρόβιλος 6 , small pine-cone, Dsc. Eup. 2.112 , Sor. 1.123 , PLit.Lond. 171 (iii A.D.); ς. μεγάλα POxy. 1142.6 (iii A.D.). cone-shaped ear-ring, Com.Adesp. 1154 .

ἀντερῶ, fut. without any pres. in use: pf. ἀντείρηκα S. Ant. 47 (cf. ἀντεῖπον):—speak against, gainsay, S.l.c.; τεθνάναι δ' οὐκέτ' ἀ. θεοῖς A. Ag. 539 ; τι πρός τινα Ar. Nu. 1079 ; πρός τι Ach. 701 ; τινί Pl. R. 580a :— Pass. , οὐδὲν ἀντειρήσεται no denial…

στύω, fut. στύσω [ῡ] AP 10.100 ( Antiphan. ): aor.1 inf. στῦσαι Ar. Lys. 598 :—make stiff or erect: sens. obsc., penem erigere, Ar. l.c.:— Pass. (with intr. pf. Act. ἔστῡκα Id. Av. 557 , Lys. 989 , Lacon. 3 pl. -αντι ib. 996 ), Id. Av. 1256 ; ἐπίτινα Luc.…
συγγεν-εύς, έως, ὁ,= συγγενής, only in dat. pl., JHS 22.358 (Pisidia), LXX 1 Ma. 10.89 cod. A, Ev.Marc. 6.4 , Ev.Luc. 2.44 .
associate, keep company with, hold converse with
συγγνωμον-έω, later form for συγγιγνώσκω Iv, Apollod. 2.7.6 , J. AJ 11.5.3 , PGnom. 161 (ii A.D., Pass. ), S.E. M. 1.126 , etc.
one who collects and writes down historic facts, historian
that which is written, writing, book
draw up a form of motion

συγκᾰλέω, fut. -καλέω Hom. Epigr. 14.8 , Att. -καλῶ X. An. 3.1.46 : call to council, convoke, convene, Il. 2.55 , A. Supp. 517 , Hdt. 1.206 , Ar. Av. 201 , X. l.c., etc.; τὰς γυναῖκας ἐπί τι Ar. Lys. 22 ; ς. τινὰς παρεῖναι Luc. Vit.Auct. 1 :— Med. , Hdt.…
to be in motion together with
bring together under one head, sum up, make a summary of
Σ. OGI 479.4 (Dorylaeum, ii A.D.): cf. συγκλείς. πρὸς τὴν ς. dub. sens. in PTeb. 5.197 (ii B.C.).
go for the purpose of meeting
confer honour on, to be an ornament to
throw into a ferment, confound utterly
get out of the way, make way
receive at the same time, enjoy together
come to an agreement, come to terms
come to pass, fall out, happen
to be an ally, to be in alliance

συμμᾰ́χ-ομαι, fut. -οῦμαι X. An. 5.4.10 : aor. συνεμαχεσάμην Aeschin. 2.169 :—fight along with others, to be an ally, auxiliary, Th. 4.44 , 8.26 , Pl. Lg. 699a , X. HG 3.2.13 : c. dat., Id. An. 5.4.10 , 6.1.13 ; τὸ οἰκὸς ἐμοὶ συμμάχεται probability is on my…
partake of with, take part in with
in measure with, proportionable, exactly suitable
in all, amounting to a total of
the room in which such parties were given
anything that happens, a chance, occurrence
happen, turn out, occur, come to pass

σύμφημι, fut. -φήσω Pl. Prt. 357b , al.: aor. 1 συνέφησα Id. R. 342e , Sph. 236d , al.: aor. 2 συνέφην freq. in Pl. (v. infr.), Elean συνέφα Schwyzer 416.5 :—assent, approve, or agree fully, A. Pr. 40 , S. Ph. 1310 , etc.; ξύμφημι κἀγώ Id. El. 1257 ; ξ. δή…
with, along with, together, at the same time

συνᾰγείρω, aor. συνήγειρα, Ep. ξυνάγειρα Il. 20.21 : Ep. 3 pl. aor.1 Pass. συνάγερθεν Theoc. 22.76 :—gather together, assemble, ὧν ἕνεκα ξυνάγειρα (sc. τοὺς θεούς) Il. l.c., cf. Pl. Criti. 121c ; ἐκκλησίην Hdt. 3.142 , cf. 1.206 ; τὸν Ὀλυμπικὸν . . ἀγῶνα, ἵνα…

συναιν-έω, fut. -αινέσω S. El. 402 : aor. -ῄνεσα A. Ag. 484 (lyr.):—consent, abs., ib. 1208 , S. Ph. 122 , El. 1280 (lyr.), Pl. R. 393e , etc.; ς. τισί agree with, Hdt. 5.92 .ή, cf. S. El. 402 , Sor. 1.58 , al.:— Med. , Inscr.Prien. 85 (ii B.C.). c. acc.,…

συνάπᾱς [ᾰπ], ᾱσα, ᾰν, = σύμπας , strengthd. for πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν, all together, mostly in pl., with or without Art., Hdt. 1.98 , 134 , 178 , 5.49 , 9.29 ; αἱ συνάπασαι ἐπιστῆμαι Pl. Phlb. 13e , etc. in sg., with collective Nouns, τὸ ς. στράτευμα Hdt. 7.187 ;…
συναρμόζω, Att. συνᾰριθμ-όττω Pl. Ti. 32b , etc.: Dor. aor.
seem to one as to another, seem good also
